rules.rule_name: Open Transaction File Browse from Starting Transaction ID
rules.rule_description: When loading a forward page of transactions, the system opens a browse session on the Transaction file starting at the specified Transaction ID as the entry point for sequential forward reading.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Open Browse on TRANSACT File Starting from given Transaction ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Transaction ID has been established as the starting point (either from a user search entry, LOW-VALUES for beginning of file, or the last Transaction ID from the current page for PF8 navigation)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initiates a forward page data loading operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system opens a browse session on the TRANSACT file positioned at the given Transaction ID, enabling sequential forward reading from that position

rules.rule_name: Skip Starting Record on PF8 Forward Navigation
rules.rule_description: When the user navigates forward using PF8, the system skips the record at the current browse position (the last transaction of the previous page) before loading new records, ensuring no duplicate transactions appear across pages.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Navigating from PF8 or New Search? / Skip Current Record Move past the starting Transaction ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: A forward page data load has been initiated and the browse session is open on the TRANSACT file
acceptance_criteria.When: The navigation was triggered by the PF8 key (forward scroll) — meaning the key pressed is NOT ENTER, NOT PF7, and NOT PF3
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system reads and discards the next record from the TRANSACT file (skipping the starting Transaction ID record) before beginning to populate the page, so that the starting transaction is not duplicated on the new page

rules.rule_name: Load New Page Without Skipping on ENTER or New Search
rules.rule_description: When the user initiates a new transaction search by pressing ENTER (including the initial program load), the system does not skip any record and begins loading transactions directly from the browse starting position.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Navigating from PF8 or New Search? / Enter or New Search

acceptance_criteria.Given: A forward page data load has been initiated and the browse session is open on the TRANSACT file
acceptance_criteria.When: The navigation was triggered by the ENTER key, PF7 key, or PF3 key (i.e., not a PF8 forward scroll)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system does NOT skip any record and proceeds directly to clearing the display rows and loading transactions from the current browse position

rules.rule_name: Clear All Transaction Display Rows Before Loading
rules.rule_description: Before populating the transaction list page with new data, all 10 transaction display rows on the screen are cleared to spaces, ensuring no stale data from a previous page remains visible.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear All 10 Transaction Display Rows on Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: A forward page data load is in progress and the skip-record step (if applicable) has been completed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is about to begin reading and populating transaction records onto the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: All 10 transaction display rows are cleared — each row's Transaction ID, Transaction Date, Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount fields are set to spaces before any new data is loaded

rules.rule_name: Sequential Forward Reading of Up to 10 Transaction Records
rules.rule_description: The system reads transaction records sequentially forward from the TRANSACT file, one at a time, continuing until either 10 records have been successfully loaded onto the page or no more records exist in the file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Row Counter ≤ 10 AND More Records Exist? / Read Next Transaction Record from TRANSACT File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The transaction display rows have been cleared and the row counter is set to 1
acceptance_criteria.When: The row counter is less than or equal to 10 AND the end of the transaction file has not been reached AND no error condition exists
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system reads the next transaction record sequentially forward from the TRANSACT file and attempts to populate it into the current row position on the screen

rules.rule_name: Capture First Transaction ID of the Page
rules.rule_description: The Transaction ID of the first record loaded onto the page is captured and stored as the page's first Transaction ID, which is used as the reference point for backward navigation (PF7) to return to this page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Row = 1? / Capture Transaction ID as First Transaction ID of Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been successfully read from the TRANSACT file during forward page loading
acceptance_criteria.When: The current row counter equals 1 (i.e., this is the first transaction being placed on the page)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID of this record is stored as the First Transaction ID of the current page (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST), in addition to being placed into the first row of the screen display

rules.rule_name: Capture Last Transaction ID of the Page
rules.rule_description: The Transaction ID of the tenth (last) record loaded onto the page is captured and stored as the page's last Transaction ID, which is used as the reference point for forward navigation (PF8) to advance to the next page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Row = 10? / Capture Transaction ID as Last Transaction ID of Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been successfully read from the TRANSACT file during forward page loading
acceptance_criteria.When: The current row counter equals 10 (i.e., this is the tenth and final transaction being placed on the page)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID of this record is stored as the Last Transaction ID of the current page (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST), in addition to being placed into the tenth row of the screen display

rules.rule_name: Format Transaction Date to MM/DD/YY for Display
rules.rule_description: The transaction's original timestamp stored in the system is reformatted into a user-friendly MM/DD/YY date format before being displayed on the transaction list screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format Transaction Date to MM/DD/YY

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been successfully read and its original timestamp (TRAN-ORIG-TS) is available
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is preparing the transaction data for display on the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction date is extracted from the original timestamp, with the year component taking only the last 2 digits (YY), and the date is formatted as MM/DD/YY (month, day, 2-digit year) for display in the transaction row's date field

rules.rule_name: Format Transaction Amount for Display
rules.rule_description: The raw transaction amount from the file is formatted with appropriate sign and decimal representation before being placed into the screen display field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format Transaction Amount with Sign and Decimal

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been successfully read and its amount (TRAN-AMT) is available
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is preparing the transaction data for display on the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction amount (TRAN-AMT) is moved into the formatted working storage amount field (WS-TRAN-AMT) which applies the defined numeric display format including sign and decimal positions, and this formatted value is placed into the screen row's amount field

rules.rule_name: Populate Transaction Row on Screen with All Four Data Fields
rules.rule_description: Each successfully read transaction record is displayed on the screen with all four data elements — Transaction ID, Transaction Date, Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount — placed into the corresponding fields of the appropriate screen row.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place Transaction ID, Date, Description and Amount into Screen Row

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read and its date and amount have been formatted
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the screen row corresponding to the current row counter (1 through 10)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID (TRAN-ID), formatted Transaction Date (WS-TRAN-DATE in MM/DD/YY), Transaction Description (TRAN-DESC), and formatted Transaction Amount (WS-TRAN-AMT) are all placed into the respective screen display fields for that row number (e.g., TRNID01I, TDATE01I, TDESC01I, TAMT001I for row 1 through TRNID10I, TDATE10I, TDESC10I, TAMT010I for row 10)

rules.rule_name: Increment Row Counter After Each Successful Record Load
rules.rule_description: After each transaction record is successfully read and placed onto the screen, the row counter is incremented by 1 to advance to the next available display row, controlling the loop that fills up to 10 rows.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Increment Row Counter by 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been successfully read and all four data fields have been populated into the current screen row
acceptance_criteria.When: The population of the current row is complete
acceptance_criteria.Then: The row counter (WS-IDX) is incremented by 1, and the system loops back to check whether the row counter is still within the 10-row limit and whether more records exist in the file

rules.rule_name: Peek-Ahead Read to Determine If Next Page Exists
rules.rule_description: After loading up to 10 transaction records onto the current page, the system attempts to read one additional record from the file solely to determine whether more transactions exist beyond the current page, enabling or disabling the forward navigation (PF8) option.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read One Additional Record to Check for Next Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has finished loading records onto the current page (either 10 records were loaded or the end of file was reached) AND at least one record was successfully loaded onto the page
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a peek-ahead by attempting to read one more record from the TRANSACT file
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the additional record is found, the system marks that a next page is available (NEXT-PAGE-YES), enabling PF8 forward navigation; if no additional record is found (end of file), the system marks that no next page is available (NEXT-PAGE-NO), disabling PF8 forward navigation

rules.rule_name: Mark No Next Page When No Records Were Loaded
rules.rule_description: If no transaction records were loaded onto the current page at all (the file was empty or the starting position was at end of file), the system marks that no next page is available without performing a peek-ahead read.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Were any records loaded onto page? / No records loaded

acceptance_criteria.Given: The forward page loading loop has completed
acceptance_criteria.When: The row counter (WS-IDX) is still at 1, meaning no records were successfully read and placed onto the page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks that no next page is available (NEXT-PAGE-NO) and skips the peek-ahead read, proceeding directly to incrementing the page number

rules.rule_name: Increment Page Number After Forward Page Load
rules.rule_description: After completing the forward page data loading (regardless of whether a full page of 10 records was loaded or fewer), the current page number is incremented by 1 to reflect the newly displayed page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Increment Page Number by 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The forward page data loading has completed, the peek-ahead check has been performed (if applicable), and the next-page availability flag has been set
acceptance_criteria.When: At least one record was loaded onto the page (WS-IDX is greater than 1)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The page number (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by 1 and the updated page number is moved to the page number display field (PAGENUMI) on the screen

rules.rule_name: Close Transaction File Browse After Page Load
rules.rule_description: After all transaction records for the current page have been read and the peek-ahead check has been completed, the browse session on the TRANSACT file is closed to release the file resources.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Close Browse on TRANSACT File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The forward page data loading loop and peek-ahead check have both completed and the page number has been updated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system has finished all required reads from the TRANSACT file for this page load operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The browse session on the TRANSACT file is ended (ENDBR), releasing the file browse position

rules.rule_name: Display Updated Transaction List Screen
rules.rule_description: After all transaction data has been loaded, formatted, and the page number updated, the transaction list screen is sent to the user displaying the populated transaction rows, current page number, header information, and any applicable messages.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Updated Transaction List Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The TRANSACT file browse has been closed and all screen fields (transaction rows, page number, header with current date and time, program name, transaction name) have been populated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is ready to present the updated transaction list to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction list screen (COTRN0A from mapset COTRN00) is sent to the user with the Transaction ID search input field cleared (set to spaces), displaying up to 10 transaction rows each containing Transaction ID, Date (MM/DD/YY), Description, and Amount, along with the current page number and any informational or error messages

sub_functionalities.title: Skip Current Record
sub_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([17.1: Skip Current Record\nStart])
    B{Which key was pressed?}
    C[Read Next Record from TRANSACT File\nAdvance past the starting Transaction ID\nso it is not repeated on the new page]
    D[Do NOT skip\nStart populating page\nfrom the current position]
    E([Proceed to Load\nUp to 10 Transactions\nfor Current Page])

    A --> B
    B -->|Key is PF8 or other\nnot Enter, PF7, or PF3| C
    B -->|Key is Enter, PF7, or PF3| D
    C --> E
    D --> E

rules.rule_name: Skip Starting Transaction ID When Scrolling Forward via PF8
rules.rule_description: When a user navigates forward through the transaction list using PF8, the system uses the last Transaction ID from the current page as the starting browse position. To avoid displaying that same transaction again at the top of the next page, the system advances past it by reading the next record before beginning to populate the new page. When the user presses ENTER or PF7 (or PF3), no skip occurs and the page is populated starting from the current browse position.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 17.1: Skip Current Record - Move past the starting Transaction ID based on navigation context (condition: key pressed is NOT Enter, PF7, or PF3)

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction List screen is active, a browse of the Transaction file has been successfully started using the reference Transaction ID (last Transaction ID from the current page when PF8 is pressed, or first Transaction ID when navigating forward from ENTER), and the system is about to load up to 10 transactions for the new page
acceptance_criteria.When: The key pressed by the user is NOT ENTER, NOT PF7, and NOT PF3 (i.e., the user pressed PF8 to scroll forward to the next page)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system reads and discards the next transaction record from the Transaction file, advancing the browse position past the starting Transaction ID, so that the transaction already seen at the bottom of the previous page is not repeated at the top of the new page; after this skip, the system proceeds to populate up to 10 transaction rows for the new page

key_functionalities.title: Backward Page Data Loading
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Backward Page Load]) --> B[Start Browse on TRANSACT File\nfrom First Transaction ID of Current Page]
    B --> C{Browse Started\nSuccessfully?}
    C -->|No| Z([End: Show Error Message])
    C -->|Yes| D[Read One Record Backward\nto Move Past Current Boundary Record]
    D --> E{Record Found?}
    E -->|No - Reached Beginning of File| Z2([End: Show Top of File Message])
    E -->|Yes| F[Clear All 10 Transaction\nDisplay Rows on Screen]
    F --> G[Set Row Index = 10\nStart filling from bottom row]
    G --> H{Row Index > 0\nAND Records Available?}
    H -->|No - Page Filled or No More Records| I{Were Any Records\nLoaded?}
    H -->|Yes| J[Read Next Record Backward\nfrom TRANSACT File]
    J --> K{Record Found?}
    K -->|No - Beginning of File Reached| I
    K -->|Yes| L[Format Transaction Date\nfrom Timestamp to MM/DD/YY]
    L --> M[Format Transaction Amount\nwith Sign and Decimal]
    M --> N[Populate Screen Row with\nTransaction ID, Date, Description, Amount]
    N --> O{Row Index = 1?\nFirst Row on Screen}
    O -->|Yes| P[Record as FIRST Transaction ID\non Current Page]
    O -->|No| Q{Row Index = 10?\nLast Row on Screen}
    Q -->|Yes| R[Record as LAST Transaction ID\non Current Page]
    Q -->|No| S[Decrement Row Index by 1]
    P --> S
    R --> S
    S --> H
    I -->|Yes| T[Attempt One More Backward Read\nto Check if Previous Page Exists]
    T --> U{Another Record\nFound?}
    U -->|Yes - Previous Page Exists| V[Decrement Page Number by 1]
    U -->|No - Already at First Page| W[Set Page Number to 1]
    V --> X[End Browse on TRANSACT File]
    W --> X
    X --> Y[Update Page Number on Screen\nand Display Updated Transaction List]
    Y --> Z3([End: Backward Page Load Complete])

rules.rule_name: Initiate Backward Browse from First Transaction ID of Current Page
rules.rule_description: When navigating to the previous page, the system initiates a backward browse of the transaction file starting from the first transaction ID that was recorded on the current page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Start Browse on TRANSACT File from First Transaction ID of Current Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction List screen and has pressed PF7 to navigate to the previous page, and the first transaction ID of the current page is available
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initiates a browse on the Transaction file using the first transaction ID of the current page as the starting position
acceptance_criteria.Then: The browse is successfully positioned at the first transaction ID of the current page, ready for backward reading; if the transaction ID is blank or null, the browse starts from the lowest available transaction in the file

rules.rule_name: Handle Browse Initiation Failure on Backward Navigation
rules.rule_description: If the transaction file browse cannot be initiated during backward page navigation, the system stops processing and displays an error message to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Browse Started Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to start a browse on the Transaction file from the first transaction ID of the current page
acceptance_criteria.When: The browse initiation fails due to an unexpected error (not a normal or not-found response)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the message 'Unable to lookup transaction...' on the Transaction List screen, and does not attempt to load any transaction records

rules.rule_name: Skip Boundary Record Before Loading Previous Page
rules.rule_description: Before loading the previous page of transactions, the system reads one record backward to move past the boundary record (the first record of the current page), so that the previous page contains records that precede the current page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read One Record Backward to Move Past Current Boundary Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The browse has been successfully initiated on the Transaction file at the first transaction ID of the current page, and the key pressed was not ENTER or PF8
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs one backward read to advance past the current boundary record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The file position moves one record backward past the starting transaction ID, so the subsequent page-fill reads retrieve records from the previous page

rules.rule_name: Handle Beginning of File Reached When Skipping Boundary Record
rules.rule_description: If the backward read to skip the boundary record reaches the beginning of the transaction file, the system notifies the user that no previous records are available.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Found? No - Reached Beginning of File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has initiated a browse and attempted one backward read to skip the boundary record
acceptance_criteria.When: The backward read returns an end-of-file condition, indicating the beginning of the transaction file has been reached
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the end-of-file indicator to TRUE, displays the message 'You have reached the top of the page...' on the Transaction List screen, and stops loading records for the previous page

rules.rule_name: Clear All Transaction Display Rows Before Loading Previous Page
rules.rule_description: Before populating the screen with the previous page of transactions, all 10 transaction display rows must be cleared to blank values to ensure no stale data from the previous display remains visible.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear All 10 Transaction Display Rows on Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The browse has been successfully initiated and the boundary record has been skipped without reaching the beginning of the file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to load the previous page of transactions
acceptance_criteria.Then: All 10 transaction display rows on the screen are cleared, setting Transaction ID, Transaction Date, Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount fields to spaces for rows 1 through 10

rules.rule_name: Set Row Index to 10 for Bottom-Up Page Population
rules.rule_description: When loading a previous page of transactions by reading backward, the screen rows are filled from the bottom (row 10) upward to row 1, so that the transactions appear in correct chronological order on screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Row Index = 10 Start filling from bottom row

acceptance_criteria.Given: All 10 transaction display rows have been cleared and the system is ready to populate the previous page
acceptance_criteria.When: The system begins the backward page population loop
acceptance_criteria.Then: The row index is set to 10, and the system begins filling transaction data starting from the bottom row of the display, working upward toward row 1

rules.rule_name: Continue Reading Backward While Rows Remain and Records Are Available
rules.rule_description: The system continues reading transaction records backward and populating screen rows as long as there are unfilled rows remaining on the screen and transaction records are still available in the file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Row Index > 0 AND Records Available?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is in the backward page population loop with a row index starting at 10
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether to continue reading backward
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system continues reading backward and populating rows only if the row index is greater than 0 AND no end-of-file condition has been reached AND no error flag has been set; the loop stops when the row index reaches 0, end-of-file is reached, or an error occurs

rules.rule_name: Read Next Transaction Record Backward from Transaction File
rules.rule_description: During backward page population, the system reads the next available transaction record in reverse order from the transaction file to populate the current screen row.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read Next Record Backward from TRANSACT File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The backward page population loop is active, the row index is greater than 0, and no end-of-file or error condition exists
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a backward read on the Transaction file
acceptance_criteria.Then: If successful, the transaction record containing Transaction ID, Transaction Date (as original timestamp), Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount is retrieved and made available for display; if end-of-file is reached, the end-of-file indicator is set to TRUE and the message 'You have reached the top of the page...' is displayed

rules.rule_name: Format Transaction Date from Timestamp to MM/DD/YY Display Format
rules.rule_description: The transaction's original timestamp stored in the system must be converted to a user-friendly MM/DD/YY date format before being displayed on the transaction list screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format Transaction Date from Timestamp to MM/DD/YY

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been successfully read from the Transaction file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the transaction date for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system extracts the year (last 2 digits), month (MM), and day (DD) from the transaction's original timestamp and formats them as MM/DD/YY for display in the transaction date field on the screen

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Row with Transaction Details
rules.rule_description: Each successfully read transaction record is displayed on the corresponding screen row with its Transaction ID, formatted date, description, and amount.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Populate Screen Row with Transaction ID, Date, Description, Amount

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read and the transaction date has been formatted to MM/DD/YY
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the screen row corresponding to the current row index (1 through 10)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID, formatted Transaction Date (MM/DD/YY), Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount are placed into the screen display fields for the row matching the current row index value

rules.rule_name: Record First Transaction ID When Populating Row 1
rules.rule_description: When the transaction data is placed into row 1 of the screen (the topmost row), the system records that transaction's ID as the first transaction ID of the current page, which will be used as the reference point for future backward navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Row Index = 1? First Row on Screen → Record as FIRST Transaction ID on Current Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is populating transaction rows during backward page load and the current row index equals 1
acceptance_criteria.When: The system places transaction data into screen row 1
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID of that record is saved as the FIRST Transaction ID of the current page (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST), to be used as the starting reference point when the user subsequently presses PF7 to go to the previous page

rules.rule_name: Record Last Transaction ID When Populating Row 10
rules.rule_description: When the transaction data is placed into row 10 of the screen (the bottommost row), the system records that transaction's ID as the last transaction ID of the current page, which will be used as the reference point for future forward navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Row Index = 10? Last Row on Screen → Record as LAST Transaction ID on Current Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is populating transaction rows during backward page load and the current row index equals 10
acceptance_criteria.When: The system places transaction data into screen row 10
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID of that record is saved as the LAST Transaction ID of the current page (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST), to be used as the starting reference point when the user subsequently presses PF8 to go to the next page

rules.rule_name: Decrement Row Index After Each Backward Record Population
rules.rule_description: After each transaction record is successfully read and placed into a screen row during backward page loading, the row index is decremented by 1 to move to the next row upward on the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Decrement Row Index by 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been successfully read and populated into the screen row at the current row index during backward page loading
acceptance_criteria.When: The system completes populating the current screen row
acceptance_criteria.Then: The row index is decremented by 1 (e.g., from 10 to 9, from 9 to 8, continuing down to 1), so the next backward read will populate the row above the current one

rules.rule_name: Check for Previous Page Existence After Filling Current Page
rules.rule_description: After all available transaction records have been loaded for the current page display, the system attempts one additional backward read to determine whether a further previous page of transactions exists.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Attempt One More Backward Read to Check if Previous Page Exists

acceptance_criteria.Given: The backward page population loop has completed (either 10 rows are filled or end-of-file was reached) and at least one record was loaded
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs one additional backward read on the Transaction file
acceptance_criteria.Then: If a record is found, it confirms that more transactions exist before the current page; if end-of-file is reached, it confirms the current page is the first page of the transaction list

rules.rule_name: Decrement Page Number When Previous Page Exists
rules.rule_description: When the system confirms that more transaction records exist before the current page and the current page number is greater than 1, the page number is decremented by 1 to reflect the correct page position after backward navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Another Record Found? Yes - Previous Page Exists → Decrement Page Number by 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The additional backward read after filling the page found another record, confirming a previous page exists, and the NEXT-PAGE flag is set to YES and the current page number is greater than 1
acceptance_criteria.When: The system updates the page number after backward navigation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The page number is decremented by 1 (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM = CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM - 1) to reflect the user has moved one page backward

rules.rule_name: Set Page Number to 1 When Already at First Page
rules.rule_description: When backward navigation reaches the beginning of the transaction file or the page number cannot be decremented further, the page number is set to 1 to indicate the user is viewing the first page of the transaction list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No - Already at First Page → Set Page Number to 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The additional backward read after filling the page did not find another record (beginning of file reached), OR the NEXT-PAGE flag is YES but the current page number is not greater than 1
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines the current page is the first page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The page number is set to 1 (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM = 1) to indicate the user is on the first page of the transaction list

rules.rule_name: End Browse and Display Updated Transaction List with Page Number
rules.rule_description: After completing the backward page load, the system closes the transaction file browse, updates the page number displayed on screen, and sends the refreshed transaction list to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Update Page Number on Screen and Display Updated Transaction List

acceptance_criteria.Given: The backward page population is complete, the page number has been updated, and the browse on the Transaction file is still open
acceptance_criteria.When: The system finalizes the backward page load
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system closes the browse on the Transaction file, moves the updated page number to the screen page number field (PAGENUMI), and displays the Transaction List screen with the updated transaction records and page number

sub_functionalities.title: Read One Record Backward to Move Past Current Boundary Record based on navigation context (condition: key pressed is NOT Enter or PF8)
sub_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Backward Page Navigation])
    B[Position browse cursor\nat First Transaction ID\nof current page]
    C{Which key\nwas pressed?}
    D[Skip initial boundary record\nRead one record backward\nto move past current page boundary]
    E[Proceed to load\nprevious page records]
    F([Continue: Clear rows\nand fill page backward])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C -->|PF7: Navigate Backward| D
    D --> E
    C -->|Enter or PF8\nNot applicable here| E
    E --> F

rules.rule_name: Set Backward Browse Starting Position to First Transaction of Current Page
rules.rule_description: When the user navigates backward (PF7), the system must position the transaction file browse cursor at the first transaction ID that was displayed on the current page, so that backward reading begins from the correct reference point. If no first transaction ID is recorded, the system defaults to the beginning of the transaction file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Position browse cursor at First Transaction ID of current page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing a page of transactions on the Transaction List screen, and the system has retained the Transaction ID of the first record displayed on the current page (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF7 to navigate to the previous page
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the first Transaction ID of the current page is available (not spaces or null), the system sets the browse starting position (TRAN-ID) to that first Transaction ID; if the first Transaction ID is blank or null, the system sets the browse starting position to the beginning of the transaction file (LOW-VALUES), and in both cases the browse cursor is positioned at that starting point in the transaction file

rules.rule_name: Skip Boundary Record When Navigating Backward via PF7
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF7 to go to the previous page, the browse cursor is initially positioned at the first transaction of the current page (which is a boundary record already seen). The system must read one record backward past this boundary record before beginning to load the previous page's transactions, ensuring the current page's first record is not re-displayed on the previous page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Skip initial boundary record
Read one record backward
to move past current page boundary

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction List screen viewing a page of transactions, the browse cursor has been positioned at the first Transaction ID of the current page, and no errors have occurred during browse positioning
acceptance_criteria.When: The key pressed is PF7 (i.e., the key pressed is NOT Enter and NOT PF8)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system reads one record backward from the current browse position to move past the boundary record (the first record of the current page), so that subsequent backward reads will load the correct set of transactions belonging to the previous page

rules.rule_name: Bypass Boundary Skip When Navigation Context Is Not PF7
rules.rule_description: The decision to skip the boundary record during backward page navigation is conditional on the key that triggered the navigation. If the navigation was triggered by Enter or PF8 (not PF7), the system does not perform the backward boundary skip and proceeds directly to loading the previous page records from the current browse position.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Which key
was pressed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The backward page navigation process has been initiated and the browse cursor has been successfully positioned at the reference Transaction ID with no errors
acceptance_criteria.When: The key pressed by the user is Enter (DFHENTER) or PF8 (DFHPF8)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system does NOT read a backward boundary record and instead proceeds directly to clearing the transaction display rows and loading up to 10 transactions backward from the current browse position

key_functionalities.title: Transaction Data Initialization
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Clear Transaction Display Rows])
    B[Begin Loop\nRow Index = 1]
    C{Row Index\n> 10?}
    D[Clear Transaction ID\nfor Current Row]
    E[Clear Transaction Date\nfor Current Row]
    F[Clear Transaction Description\nfor Current Row]
    G[Clear Transaction Amount\nfor Current Row]
    H[Move to Next Row\nRow Index = Row Index + 1]
    I([End: All 10 Rows Cleared\nReady for New Data])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C -->|No - Continue Clearing| D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    G --> H
    H --> C
    C -->|Yes - All Rows Cleared| I

rules.rule_name: Clear All Transaction Display Rows Before Loading New Page Data
rules.rule_description: Before displaying a new page of transactions (either forward or backward navigation), all 10 transaction display rows on the Transaction List screen must be completely cleared — including Transaction ID, Transaction Date, Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount — to ensure no stale data from a previous page remains visible to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transaction Data Initialization - Clear all 10 transaction display rows (ID, date, description, amount) on the screen before populating with new data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display a new page of transactions on the Transaction List screen, triggered either by a forward page navigation (ENTER or PF8) or a backward page navigation (PF7), and the transaction file browse has been successfully initiated without errors
acceptance_criteria.When: The system iterates through all 10 display rows (Row Index 1 through 10 inclusive, incrementing by 1 each iteration) before populating them with new transaction data
acceptance_criteria.Then: For each of the 10 rows, the system clears all four display fields to spaces: Transaction ID (TRNIDnnI), Transaction Date (TDATEnnI), Transaction Description (TDESCnnI), and Transaction Amount (TAMTnnnI), so that all 10 rows are blank and ready to receive fresh transaction data from the file

rules.rule_name: Clear Transaction ID Field for Each Display Row
rules.rule_description: As part of the screen refresh process, the Transaction ID field for each of the 10 display rows must be individually set to spaces before new transaction data is loaded, ensuring no previously displayed Transaction ID remains on screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear Transaction ID for Current Row

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is iterating through display rows 1 to 10 to clear the Transaction List screen in preparation for a new page of data
acceptance_criteria.When: The current row index is any value from 1 to 10 (WHEN 1 through WHEN 10 in the row evaluation)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID field for that specific row (TRNID01I through TRNID10I of COTRN0AI) is set to SPACES, removing any previously displayed transaction identifier for that row

rules.rule_name: Clear Transaction Date Field for Each Display Row
rules.rule_description: As part of the screen refresh process, the Transaction Date field for each of the 10 display rows must be individually set to spaces before new transaction data is loaded, ensuring no previously displayed Transaction Date remains on screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear Transaction Date for Current Row

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is iterating through display rows 1 to 10 to clear the Transaction List screen in preparation for a new page of data
acceptance_criteria.When: The current row index is any value from 1 to 10 (WHEN 1 through WHEN 10 in the row evaluation)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Date field for that specific row (TDATE01I through TDATE10I of COTRN0AI) is set to SPACES, removing any previously displayed transaction date for that row

rules.rule_name: Clear Transaction Description Field for Each Display Row
rules.rule_description: As part of the screen refresh process, the Transaction Description field for each of the 10 display rows must be individually set to spaces before new transaction data is loaded, ensuring no previously displayed Transaction Description remains on screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear Transaction Description for Current Row

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is iterating through display rows 1 to 10 to clear the Transaction List screen in preparation for a new page of data
acceptance_criteria.When: The current row index is any value from 1 to 10 (WHEN 1 through WHEN 10 in the row evaluation)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Description field for that specific row (TDESC01I through TDESC10I of COTRN0AI) is set to SPACES, removing any previously displayed transaction description for that row

rules.rule_name: Clear Transaction Amount Field for Each Display Row
rules.rule_description: As part of the screen refresh process, the Transaction Amount field for each of the 10 display rows must be individually set to spaces before new transaction data is loaded, ensuring no previously displayed Transaction Amount remains on screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear Transaction Amount for Current Row

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is iterating through display rows 1 to 10 to clear the Transaction List screen in preparation for a new page of data
acceptance_criteria.When: The current row index is any value from 1 to 10 (WHEN 1 through WHEN 10 in the row evaluation)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Amount field for that specific row (TAMT001I through TAMT010I of COTRN0AI) is set to SPACES, removing any previously displayed transaction amount for that row

rules.rule_name: Advance to Next Row After Clearing Current Row
rules.rule_description: The screen clearing process iterates sequentially through all 10 display rows. After clearing all four fields of the current row, the row index is incremented by 1 to move to the next row, continuing until all 10 rows have been cleared.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Move to Next Row - Row Index = Row Index + 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has just cleared all four display fields (Transaction ID, Transaction Date, Transaction Description, Transaction Amount) for the current row during the screen initialization loop
acceptance_criteria.When: The current row index is any value from 1 to 9 (i.e., row index is not yet greater than 10)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The row index is incremented by 1 (Row Index = Row Index + 1) and the system proceeds to clear the fields of the next row, continuing the loop until the row index exceeds 10, at which point all 10 rows have been cleared and the screen is ready for new transaction data

rules.rule_name: Screen Clearing Triggered During Forward Page Navigation
rules.rule_description: When navigating forward through the transaction list (via ENTER key or PF8), the system must clear all 10 display rows before populating them with the next set of transactions, provided the transaction file browse was initiated successfully and no errors have occurred.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Begin Loop - Row Index = 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has triggered a forward page navigation (by pressing ENTER or PF8) on the Transaction List screen, and the transaction file browse has been successfully started without any errors (ERR-FLG is OFF) and the end-of-file condition has not been reached (TRANSACT-NOT-EOF is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system begins the page-forward process and is ready to populate the display rows with new transaction data
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system initiates a loop starting at Row Index = 1, incrementing by 1 until Row Index exceeds 10, calling the row-clearing routine (INITIALIZE-TRAN-DATA) for each row, resulting in all 10 transaction display rows being cleared before any new data is populated

rules.rule_name: Screen Clearing Triggered During Backward Page Navigation
rules.rule_description: When navigating backward through the transaction list (via PF7), the system must clear all 10 display rows before populating them with the previous set of transactions, provided the transaction file browse was initiated successfully and no errors have occurred.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Begin Loop - Row Index = 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has triggered a backward page navigation (by pressing PF7) on the Transaction List screen, and the transaction file browse has been successfully started without any errors (ERR-FLG is OFF) and the end-of-file condition has not been reached (TRANSACT-NOT-EOF is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system begins the page-backward process and is ready to populate the display rows with the previous page's transaction data
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system initiates a loop starting at Row Index = 1, incrementing by 1 until Row Index exceeds 10, calling the row-clearing routine (INITIALIZE-TRAN-DATA) for each row, resulting in all 10 transaction display rows being cleared before any new data is populated

key_functionalities.title: Transaction Record Population
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Populate Transaction Record])
    B[Format Transaction Amount\nwith sign and decimal notation]
    C[Extract Transaction Origination Timestamp\nReformat to MM/DD/YY display format]
    D{Which Screen Row?\nCheck Row Index 1 to 10}
    E[Row 1:\nPlace Transaction ID, Date,\nDescription, Amount\nAlso record as FIRST Transaction ID\nfor backward pagination]
    F[Rows 2 to 9:\nPlace Transaction ID, Date,\nDescription, Amount\ninto corresponding screen row]
    G[Row 10:\nPlace Transaction ID, Date,\nDescription, Amount\nAlso record as LAST Transaction ID\nfor forward pagination]
    H[No Action\nRow index out of range]
    I([End: Screen Row Populated])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D -->|Row = 1| E
    D -->|Row = 2 through 9| F
    D -->|Row = 10| G
    D -->|Other| H
    E --> I
    F --> I
    G --> I
    H --> I

rules.rule_name: Format Transaction Amount for Display
rules.rule_description: When populating a transaction record onto the screen, the raw transaction amount from the transaction record must be formatted into a displayable amount value before being placed on the screen row.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Format Transaction Amount
with sign and decimal notation

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been successfully retrieved from the transaction file and contains a raw transaction amount (TRAN-AMT)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to populate a screen row with the transaction data
acceptance_criteria.Then: The raw transaction amount (TRAN-AMT) is moved into the working storage display amount field (WS-TRAN-AMT), which applies the defined sign and decimal notation formatting, making it ready for screen display

rules.rule_name: Reformat Transaction Origination Date to MM/DD/YY Display Format
rules.rule_description: The transaction origination timestamp stored in the transaction record must be extracted and reformatted from its internal timestamp format into the MM/DD/YY display format before being shown on the transaction list screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Extract Transaction Origination Timestamp
Reformat to MM/DD/YY display format

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been retrieved and contains an origination timestamp (TRAN-ORIG-TS) in internal storage format
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to populate a screen row with the transaction data
acceptance_criteria.Then: The origination timestamp is moved into the working storage timestamp field (WS-TIMESTAMP); the year component (positions 3-4 of the date portion) is extracted into WS-CURDATE-YY; the month component is extracted into WS-CURDATE-MM; the day component is extracted into WS-CURDATE-DD; and these three components are combined into the MM/DD/YY formatted display date (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY), which is then stored in WS-TRAN-DATE for screen placement

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Row 1 and Record First Transaction ID for Backward Pagination
rules.rule_description: When the first transaction slot (row 1) on the transaction list screen is being filled, the transaction details are placed into screen row 1 fields AND the transaction ID is additionally saved as the first transaction ID anchor point to support backward page navigation (PF7).
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Row 1:
Place Transaction ID, Date,
Description, Amount
Also record as FIRST Transaction ID
for backward pagination

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been retrieved, its amount has been formatted into WS-TRAN-AMT, and its date has been reformatted into WS-TRAN-DATE, and the current screen row index (WS-IDX) is 1
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the screen row for this transaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID (TRAN-ID) is placed into screen row 1 Transaction ID field (TRNID01I of COTRN0AI); the formatted date (WS-TRAN-DATE) is placed into screen row 1 date field (TDATE01I of COTRN0AI); the transaction description (TRAN-DESC) is placed into screen row 1 description field (TDESC01I of COTRN0AI); the formatted amount (WS-TRAN-AMT) is placed into screen row 1 amount field (TAMT001I of COTRN0AI); AND the Transaction ID is also saved into the pagination anchor field CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST, which is used as the starting reference point when the user navigates backward to the previous page

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Rows 2 Through 9 with Transaction Details
rules.rule_description: For transactions placed in screen rows 2 through 9, the transaction details (ID, date, description, amount) are placed into the corresponding screen row fields. No pagination anchor is recorded for these rows.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Rows 2 to 9:
Place Transaction ID, Date,
Description, Amount
into corresponding screen row

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been retrieved, its amount has been formatted into WS-TRAN-AMT, and its date has been reformatted into WS-TRAN-DATE, and the current screen row index (WS-IDX) is between 2 and 9 inclusive
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the screen row for this transaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: For the matching row index (2 through 9), the Transaction ID (TRAN-ID) is placed into the corresponding screen row Transaction ID field (TRNIDxxI of COTRN0AI); the formatted date (WS-TRAN-DATE) is placed into the corresponding screen row date field (TDATExxI of COTRN0AI); the transaction description (TRAN-DESC) is placed into the corresponding screen row description field (TDESCxxI of COTRN0AI); and the formatted amount (WS-TRAN-AMT) is placed into the corresponding screen row amount field (TAMTxxxI of COTRN0AI); no pagination anchor fields are updated for rows 2 through 9

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Row 10 and Record Last Transaction ID for Forward Pagination
rules.rule_description: When the tenth and final transaction slot (row 10) on the transaction list screen is being filled, the transaction details are placed into screen row 10 fields AND the transaction ID is additionally saved as the last transaction ID anchor point to support forward page navigation (PF8).
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Row 10:
Place Transaction ID, Date,
Description, Amount
Also record as LAST Transaction ID
for forward pagination

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been retrieved, its amount has been formatted into WS-TRAN-AMT, and its date has been reformatted into WS-TRAN-DATE, and the current screen row index (WS-IDX) is 10
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the screen row for this transaction

key_functionalities.title: Transaction Date Formatting
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Transaction Date Formatting])
    B[Read Transaction Origination\nTimestamp from Transaction Record]
    C[Extract Month MM\nfrom Timestamp]
    D[Extract Day DD\nfrom Timestamp]
    E[Extract Year YY\nLast 2 digits only from Timestamp]
    F[Assemble Date into\nMM/DD/YY Display Format]
    G([End: Formatted Date\nReady for Screen Display])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G

rules.rule_name: Load Transaction Origination Timestamp for Date Formatting
rules.rule_description: Before the transaction date can be formatted for display, the system must retrieve the transaction's original timestamp from the transaction record and stage it into a working date/time structure for subsequent field extraction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read Transaction Origination Timestamp from Transaction Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been successfully retrieved from the Transaction file, and the record contains a populated Transaction Origination Timestamp (TRAN-ORIG-TS) field representing when the transaction originally occurred
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to populate the transaction data for screen display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system copies the Transaction Origination Timestamp (TRAN-ORIG-TS) from the transaction record into the working timestamp structure (WS-TIMESTAMP), making all date and time components available for individual field extraction

rules.rule_name: Extract Month Component from Transaction Timestamp
rules.rule_description: The system extracts the two-digit Month (MM) component from the staged transaction origination timestamp to be used as part of the formatted display date.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Extract Month MM from Timestamp

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Origination Timestamp has been loaded into the working timestamp structure (WS-TIMESTAMP), and the timestamp contains a parseable Month component (WS-TIMESTAMP-DT-MM)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system extracts individual date components from the working timestamp for date reformatting
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system copies the two-digit Month value (WS-TIMESTAMP-DT-MM) from the working timestamp into the current date Month field (WS-CURDATE-MM), making it available for assembly into the final display date format

rules.rule_name: Extract Day Component from Transaction Timestamp
rules.rule_description: The system extracts the two-digit Day (DD) component from the staged transaction origination timestamp to be used as part of the formatted display date.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Extract Day DD from Timestamp

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Origination Timestamp has been loaded into the working timestamp structure (WS-TIMESTAMP), and the timestamp contains a parseable Day component (WS-TIMESTAMP-DT-DD)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system extracts individual date components from the working timestamp for date reformatting
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system copies the two-digit Day value (WS-TIMESTAMP-DT-DD) from the working timestamp into the current date Day field (WS-CURDATE-DD), making it available for assembly into the final display date format

rules.rule_name: Extract Two-Digit Year Component from Transaction Timestamp
rules.rule_description: The system extracts only the last two digits of the four-digit Year (YYYY) from the transaction origination timestamp. The first two digits (century) are discarded, and only positions 3 and 4 of the four-digit year are used to produce the two-digit year (YY) for display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Extract Year YY Last 2 digits only from Timestamp

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Origination Timestamp has been loaded into the working timestamp structure (WS-TIMESTAMP), and the timestamp contains a four-digit Year component (WS-TIMESTAMP-DT-YYYY) such as '2024'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system extracts the year component from the working timestamp for date reformatting
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system extracts only the last two characters of the four-digit year by using a substring starting at position 3 with a length of 2 (WS-TIMESTAMP-DT-YYYY(3:2)), copies this two-digit year value into the current date Year field (WS-CURDATE-YY) — for example, '2024' becomes '24' — discarding the century portion entirely

rules.rule_name: Assemble Transaction Date into MM/DD/YY Display Format
rules.rule_description: After all individual date components (Month, Day, two-digit Year) have been extracted from the transaction origination timestamp, the system assembles them into the final MM/DD/YY formatted date string that will be displayed on the Transaction List screen next to each transaction row.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Assemble Date into MM/DD/YY Display Format

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Month (WS-CURDATE-MM), Day (WS-CURDATE-DD), and two-digit Year (WS-CURDATE-YY) components have all been individually extracted from the transaction origination timestamp and are populated in their respective working fields, and these three components are combined within the composite date field WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY in MM/DD/YY order
acceptance_criteria.When: The system finalizes the transaction date value for screen display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system moves the assembled composite date (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) into the transaction display date field (WS-TRAN-DATE) in MM/DD/YY format, which is then mapped to the corresponding transaction row date field on the Transaction List screen (e.g., TDATE01I through TDATE10I depending on the row position 1–10)

rules.rule_name: Save First Transaction ID on Page as Backward Navigation Anchor
rules.rule_description: When the first row (row 1) of the transaction list page is being populated, the system must record the Transaction ID both in the first screen display row and as the page's first transaction anchor (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST), which will be used as the starting reference point when the user navigates backward using PF7.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Row 1: Place Transaction ID into Screen Row 1 AND save as First Transaction ID on Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The transaction list page is being populated and the current row index being filled is row 1
acceptance_criteria.When: A transaction record is read and assigned to display row 1 of the transaction list screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID of that record must be placed into screen display row 1 (TRNID01I) AND simultaneously saved as the First Transaction ID on the page (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST) to serve as the backward navigation anchor for PF7 scrolling

rules.rule_name: Populate Middle Transaction Rows Without Updating Navigation Anchors
rules.rule_description: When rows 2 through 9 of the transaction list page are being populated, the system places the Transaction ID only into the corresponding screen display row. No navigation anchor values are updated for these middle rows.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Rows 2-9: Place Transaction ID into corresponding Screen Row only

acceptance_criteria.Given: The transaction list page is being populated and the current row index being filled is any row between 2 and 9 (inclusive)
acceptance_criteria.When: A transaction record is read and assigned to a middle display row (rows 2 through 9) of the transaction list screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID of that record must be placed only into the corresponding screen display row field (TRNID02I through TRNID09I respectively), and neither the First Transaction ID anchor (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST) nor the Last Transaction ID anchor (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST) is updated

rules.rule_name: Save Last Transaction ID on Page as Forward Navigation Anchor
rules.rule_description: When the last row (row 10) of the transaction list page is being populated, the system must record the Transaction ID both in the tenth screen display row and as the page's last transaction anchor (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST), which will be used as the starting reference point when the user navigates forward using PF8.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Row 10: Place Transaction ID into Screen Row 10 AND save as Last Transaction ID on Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The transaction list page is being populated and the current row index being filled is row 10
acceptance_criteria.When: A transaction record is read and assigned to display row 10 of the transaction list screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID of that record must be placed into screen display row 10 (TRNID10I) AND simultaneously saved as the Last Transaction ID on the page (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST) to serve as the forward navigation anchor for PF8 scrolling

rules.rule_name: Use First Transaction ID Anchor as Starting Point for Backward Page Navigation
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF7 to scroll backward to the previous page, the system uses the saved First Transaction ID of the current page (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST) as the reference point from which to begin reading records in reverse order. If no first transaction ID has been saved, the system starts from the very beginning of the transaction file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: First Transaction ID CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST Used as starting point for PF7 Backward Navigation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the transaction list and the current page has a saved First Transaction ID (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST) from when the page was populated
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF7 to navigate to the previous page AND the current page number is greater than 1
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must use the saved First Transaction ID (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST) as the starting position (TRAN-ID) for reading records backward; if the First Transaction ID is blank or empty, the system defaults to starting from the very beginning of the transaction file (LOW-VALUES), and then proceeds to retrieve the previous page of up to 10 transactions

rules.rule_name: Use Last Transaction ID Anchor as Starting Point for Forward Page Navigation
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF8 to scroll forward to the next page, the system uses the saved Last Transaction ID of the current page (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST) as the reference point from which to begin reading records in forward order. If no last transaction ID has been saved, the system starts from the highest possible transaction value.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Last Transaction ID CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST Used as starting point for PF8 Forward Navigation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the transaction list and the current page has a saved Last Transaction ID (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST) from when the page was populated, and the next-page indicator confirms more pages are available
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF8 to navigate to the next page AND the next-page-available indicator is set to YES
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must use the saved Last Transaction ID (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST) as the starting position (TRAN-ID) for reading records forward; if the Last Transaction ID is blank or empty, the system defaults to starting from the highest possible transaction value (HIGH-VALUES), and then proceeds to retrieve the next page of up to 10 transactions

key_functionalities.title: Next Page Availability Detection
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([After Loading Current Page of Transactions])
    B{Were 10 Records\nSuccessfully Loaded?}
    C[Attempt to Read\nOne Additional Record\nBeyond Current Page]
    D{Additional Record\nFound?}
    E[Set Next Page Indicator = YES\nMore transactions available]
    F[Set Next Page Indicator = NO\nNo more transactions available]
    G{Were Any Records\nLoaded on Page?\nRow Index > 1?}
    H[Set Next Page Indicator = NO\nNo more transactions available]
    I([Proceed to Display Page])

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - Full Page Loaded| C
    C --> D
    D -->|Yes - Record Exists| E
    D -->|No - End of Transactions| F
    B -->|No - Partial or Empty Page| G
    G -->|Yes - At Least 1 Record| H
    G -->|No - No Records Loaded| H
    E --> I
    F --> I
    H --> I

rules.rule_name: Determine If Current Page Is Fully Loaded with 10 Transactions
rules.rule_description: After attempting to load transactions onto the current page, the system checks whether a full page of 10 transactions was successfully retrieved without reaching the end of the transaction file, to decide whether to probe for additional records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Were 10 Records Successfully Loaded?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed the loop to load up to 10 transactions for the current page from the transaction file
acceptance_criteria.When: The end-of-file indicator for the transaction file is NOT set (TRANSACT-NOT-EOF is true) AND no error condition is active (ERR-FLG-OFF is true) after the loading loop completes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system determines that a full page of 10 transactions has been successfully loaded and proceeds to attempt reading one additional record beyond the current page to check for more data

rules.rule_name: Probe for Additional Transaction Record Beyond Current Page
rules.rule_description: After confirming a full page of 10 transactions is loaded, the system reads one extra record from the transaction file solely to determine whether more transactions exist beyond the current page, without displaying that record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Attempt to Read One Additional Record Beyond Current Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: A full page of 10 transactions has been successfully loaded and the transaction file has not reached end-of-file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to read the next sequential transaction record from the transaction file beyond the 10th record of the current page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system uses the result of this read (success or end-of-file) exclusively to set the next-page availability indicator, and the record read is not displayed to the user

rules.rule_name: Set Next Page Available When Additional Transaction Exists
rules.rule_description: When the probe read beyond the current page successfully retrieves a record, the system marks that a next page of transactions is available, enabling the user to scroll forward.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Additional Record Found? → Yes - Record Exists → Set Next Page Indicator = YES

acceptance_criteria.Given: A full page of 10 transactions has been loaded and the system has attempted to read one additional record beyond the current page
acceptance_criteria.When: The additional read is successful — the transaction file end-of-file indicator remains NOT set (TRANSACT-NOT-EOF is true) AND no error condition is active (ERR-FLG-OFF is true)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next-page indicator is set to YES (NEXT-PAGE-YES), signaling that more transactions are available and the user may navigate forward to the next page using PF8

rules.rule_name: Set Next Page Unavailable When No Additional Transaction Exists After Full Page
rules.rule_description: When the probe read beyond a full page of 10 transactions reaches the end of the transaction file, the system marks that no further pages are available, preventing the user from attempting to scroll forward.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Additional Record Found? → No - End of Transactions → Set Next Page Indicator = NO

acceptance_criteria.Given: A full page of 10 transactions has been loaded and the system has attempted to read one additional record beyond the current page
acceptance_criteria.When: The additional read reaches the end of the transaction file — the end-of-file indicator is set (TRANSACT-EOF becomes true) OR an error condition is active
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next-page indicator is set to NO (NEXT-PAGE-NO), signaling that the current page is the last page and the user cannot navigate further forward

rules.rule_name: Set Next Page Unavailable When Partial or Empty Page Loaded
rules.rule_description: When fewer than 10 transactions are loaded (partial page) or no transactions are loaded at all (empty page), the system unconditionally marks that no next page is available, regardless of whether any records were retrieved.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Were Any Records Loaded on Page? Row Index > 1? → Set Next Page Indicator = NO

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed the loop to load up to 10 transactions and the transaction file end-of-file was reached OR an error occurred before 10 records were loaded
acceptance_criteria.When: The end-of-file indicator is set (TRANSACT-EOF is true) OR an error condition is active (ERR-FLG-ON is true), meaning fewer than 10 records were loaded — regardless of whether the row index (WS-IDX) is greater than 1 (at least 1 record loaded) or equal to 1 (no records loaded)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next-page indicator is set to NO (NEXT-PAGE-NO), signaling that no further pages exist beyond the current partial or empty page

rules.rule_name: Increment Page Number When at Least One Transaction Record Was Loaded on Partial Page
rules.rule_description: When a partial page is loaded (at least one but fewer than 10 transactions), the system still increments the page counter to reflect that the user has advanced to a new page, even though it is not fully populated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Were Any Records Loaded on Page? Row Index > 1?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The transaction file reached end-of-file or an error occurred before a full page of 10 transactions was loaded
acceptance_criteria.When: The row index (WS-IDX) is greater than 1, meaning at least one transaction record was successfully loaded onto the current page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by 1 to reflect that the user has moved to a new page, and the next-page indicator is set to NO

rules.rule_name: Increment Page Number After Successfully Loading a Full Page
rules.rule_description: When a full page of 10 transactions is confirmed as loaded, the system increments the page counter before probing for additional records, ensuring the displayed page number accurately reflects the user's current position in the transaction list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Were 10 Records Successfully Loaded? → Yes - Full Page Loaded

acceptance_criteria.Given: The loading loop has completed and the transaction file end-of-file indicator is NOT set (TRANSACT-NOT-EOF is true) AND no error condition is active (ERR-FLG-OFF is true), confirming 10 records were loaded
acceptance_criteria.When: The system confirms a full page of 10 transactions has been loaded
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by 1 (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM = CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM + 1) before the probe read is performed

key_functionalities.title: Page Number Tracking
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Page Number Tracking Start])
    B{Navigation\nDirection?}
    C{Forward: Were any\nrecords loaded?}
    D{Full page of 10\nrecords loaded?}
    E[Increment Page Number\nPage = Page + 1]
    F{Partial page loaded?\nAt least 1 record?}
    G[Increment Page Number\nPage = Page + 1]
    H[No Page Change\nNo records found]
    I{Backward: Was a\nprevious record found\nbeyond current page?}
    J{Current Page\nNumber > 1?}
    K[Decrement Page Number\nPage = Page - 1]
    L[Reset to Page 1\nPage = 1]
    M[Display Updated\nPage Number on Screen]
    N([Page Number Tracking End])

    A --> B
    B -->|PF8 Forward| C
    B -->|PF7 Backward| I
    C -->|Yes, records loaded| D
    D -->|Full page 10 records| E
    D -->|Partial page EOF reached| F
    F -->|Yes, at least 1 record| G
    F -->|No records at all| H
    C -->|No records found| H
    E --> M
    G --> M
    H --> M
    I -->|Yes, prior record exists| J
    I -->|No prior record exists| L
    J -->|Page > 1| K
    J -->|Already on Page 1| L
    K --> M
    L --> M
    M --> N

rules.rule_name: Increment Page Number When Full Page of 10 Transactions Loaded (Forward Navigation)
rules.rule_description: When navigating forward and a full page of 10 transactions is successfully retrieved from the transaction file, the current page number is incremented by 1 to reflect the new page position.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Full page of 10 records loaded? → Increment Page Number Page = Page + 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the transaction list and the current page number is tracked in the session context (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM), and the system has started a forward browse of the transaction file from the current Transaction ID position
acceptance_criteria.When: The system successfully reads and loads all 10 transaction records into the display rows (WS-IDX reaches 11, meaning the loop completed with records still available and no end-of-file condition was reached), indicating a full page was populated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number is incremented by 1 (Page = Page + 1), and the updated page number is displayed on the Transaction List screen in the page number field (PAGENUMI)

rules.rule_name: Increment Page Number When Partial Page of Transactions Loaded at End of File (Forward Navigation)
rules.rule_description: When navigating forward and the end of the transaction file is reached before filling all 10 rows, but at least 1 transaction was loaded, the page number is still incremented by 1 to reflect that a new (partial) page has been reached.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Partial page loaded? At least 1 record? → Yes, at least 1 record → Increment Page Number Page = Page + 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is navigating forward through the transaction list and the current page number is tracked in the session context (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM), and the system has started a forward browse of the transaction file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reaches the end of the transaction file before loading all 10 records (TRANSACT-EOF is set), but at least 1 transaction record was loaded into the display (WS-IDX is greater than 1, meaning the index advanced at least once from its starting value of 1)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number is incremented by 1 (Page = Page + 1), the next-page indicator is set to NO (no further forward navigation is possible), and the updated page number is displayed on the Transaction List screen in the page number field (PAGENUMI)

rules.rule_name: No Page Number Change When No Transactions Found During Forward Navigation
rules.rule_description: When navigating forward and no transaction records are found at all (end of file is reached immediately with zero records loaded), the page number remains unchanged.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No records at all → No Page Change No records found

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is navigating forward through the transaction list and the current page number is tracked in the session context (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM), and the system has started a forward browse of the transaction file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reaches the end of the transaction file immediately without loading any transaction records (TRANSACT-EOF is set and WS-IDX remains at 1, meaning no records were populated into any display row)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number is NOT incremented and remains unchanged, the next-page indicator is set to NO, and the unchanged page number is displayed on the Transaction List screen in the page number field (PAGENUMI)

rules.rule_name: Decrement Page Number When Prior Transactions Exist Beyond Current Page (Backward Navigation)
rules.rule_description: When navigating backward and there are more transactions before the current page (i.e., the user is not on the first page), the page number is decremented by 1 to reflect moving to the previous page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Yes, prior record exists → Current Page Number > 1? → Page > 1 → Decrement Page Number Page = Page - 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is navigating backward through the transaction list using PF7, and the current page number stored in the session context (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM) is greater than 1, and the system has started a backward browse of the transaction file from the first Transaction ID of the current page
acceptance_criteria.When: After loading up to 10 transactions backward into the display rows, the system successfully reads one additional previous transaction record beyond the loaded page (TRANSACT-NOT-EOF is true and no error flag is set), confirming that prior records exist before the current page, AND the current page number is greater than 1
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number is decremented by 1 (Page = Page - 1), and the updated page number is displayed on the Transaction List screen in the page number field (PAGENUMI)

rules.rule_name: Reset Page Number to 1 When Already on First Page During Backward Navigation
rules.rule_description: When navigating backward and prior records exist beyond the loaded page but the current page number is already 1, the page number is reset to 1 to ensure it never goes below the minimum value.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Yes, prior record exists → Current Page Number > 1? → Already on Page 1 → Reset to Page 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is navigating backward through the transaction list using PF7, and the current page number stored in the session context (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM) is exactly 1, and the system has started a backward browse of the transaction file
acceptance_criteria.When: After loading transactions backward, the system successfully reads one additional previous transaction record (TRANSACT-NOT-EOF is true and no error flag is set), confirming prior records exist, BUT the current page number is NOT greater than 1 (it is already at page 1)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The page number is set to 1 (Page = 1), ensuring it does not go below the minimum page value, and the page number 1 is displayed on the Transaction List screen in the page number field (PAGENUMI)

rules.rule_name: Reset Page Number to 1 When No Prior Transactions Exist During Backward Navigation
rules.rule_description: When navigating backward and no transactions exist before the currently displayed page (the beginning of the transaction file has been reached), the page number is reset to 1, confirming the user is on the first page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No prior record exists → Reset to Page 1 Page = 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is navigating backward through the transaction list using PF7, and the current page number is tracked in the session context (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM), and the system has started a backward browse of the transaction file from the first Transaction ID of the current page
acceptance_criteria.When: After loading up to 10 transactions backward into the display rows, the system attempts to read one additional previous transaction record but reaches the beginning of the file (TRANSACT-EOF is set or an error condition is encountered), confirming no prior records exist before the current page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The page number is set to 1 (Page = 1), confirming the user is on the first page, and the page number 1 is displayed on the Transaction List screen in the page number field (PAGENUMI)

rules.rule_name: Display Updated Page Number on Transaction List Screen
