rules.rule_description: After any page navigation action (forward or backward), the current page number is always displayed on the Transaction List screen so the user knows their current position in the transaction list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Updated Page Number on Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has performed a navigation action (ENTER for new search, PF7 for backward, or PF8 for forward) and the page number has been computed or adjusted accordingly in the session context (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system completes the page number calculation (increment, decrement, reset to 1, or no change) and prepares to send the Transaction List screen to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The computed page number value from the session context (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM) is moved into the page number display field (PAGENUMI) on the Transaction List screen (COTRN0AI), and the screen is sent to the user showing the correct current page number

key_functionalities.title: Return to Main Menu
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([User Presses PF3\nReturn to Main Menu])
    B[Set Destination Program\nto Main Menu - COMEN01C]
    C{Destination Program\nValid?}
    D[Default to\nSign-On Screen - COSGN00C]
    E[Record Current Program\nand Transaction ID\nin Session Data]
    F[Transfer Control to\nMain Menu Screen\nCOMEN01C\nwith Session Data]

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C -->|Destination is blank\nor invalid| D
    D --> E
    C -->|Destination is valid\nCOMEN01C| E
    E --> F

rules.rule_name: Set Main Menu as Return Destination on PF3
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF3 on the Transaction List screen, the system designates the Main Menu screen (COMEN01C) as the target destination for navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Destination Program to Main Menu - COMEN01C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction List screen with an active session
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Main Menu screen identified as 'COMEN01C'

rules.rule_name: Validate Destination Program Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to any screen, the system validates that a destination program has been properly set. If the destination is blank or uninitialized, the system defaults to the Sign-On screen to prevent navigation to an undefined target.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Destination Program Valid?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is about to transfer control to a destination program after PF3 is pressed
acceptance_criteria.When: The destination program value is evaluated and found to be blank (spaces) or uninitialized (low-values)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system overrides the destination and sets it to the Sign-On screen identified as 'COSGN00C' to ensure a valid navigation target

rules.rule_name: Default Navigation to Sign-On Screen When Destination is Invalid
rules.rule_description: As a fallback policy, when no valid destination program is defined at the time of navigation, the system routes the user to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) rather than allowing navigation to fail or reach an undefined screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Default to Sign-On Screen - COSGN00C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is processing a return-to-previous-screen request and the destination program has been found to be blank or uninitialized
acceptance_criteria.When: The destination program field contains spaces or low-values
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Sign-On screen identified as 'COSGN00C', overriding any previously blank or invalid destination value

rules.rule_name: Record Current Program and Transaction in Session Data Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to another screen, the system records the current program name and current transaction identifier into the shared session data (communication area), along with resetting the program context to zero, so the destination screen knows where the user navigated from.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Current Program and Transaction ID in Session Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has a valid destination program set (either COMEN01C or defaulted to COSGN00C) and is preparing to transfer control
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is about to execute the screen transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the current transaction identifier into the session data field 'From Transaction ID', records the current program name into the session data field 'From Program', and resets the program context indicator to zero (0) in the session data before transferring control

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Destination Screen with Session Data
rules.rule_description: After recording the originating program and transaction details, the system transfers full control to the destination screen (Main Menu COMEN01C or Sign-On COSGN00C as fallback), passing the complete session data so the destination screen has full context of the user's session.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer Control to Main Menu Screen COMEN01C with Session Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The destination program has been validated or defaulted, and the current program name, transaction ID, and program context have been recorded in the session data
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the screen transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system transfers complete control to the destination program (COMEN01C for Main Menu, or COSGN00C as fallback) and passes the full session data (communication area containing From Transaction ID, From Program, and Program Context) to the destination screen, ending execution of the current Transaction List program

key_functionalities.title: Invalid Key Handling
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([User Presses a Function Key]) --> B{Is it a Recognized\nFunction Key?\nEnter / PF3 / PF7 / PF8}
    B -->|Yes| C([Route to Appropriate Process])
    B -->|No / Unrecognized Key| D[Set Error Indicator]
    D --> E[Set Error Message:\nInvalid Key]
    E --> F[Re-Display Current\nTransaction List Screen\nwith Error Message]
    F --> G([Await Next User Action])

rules.rule_name: Detect Unrecognized Function Key Press on Transaction List Screen
rules.rule_description: When a user presses a function key that is not one of the four recognized keys (Enter, PF3, PF7, PF8) on the Transaction List screen, the system must identify it as an invalid key action and prevent any transaction list processing from occurring.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is it a Recognized Function Key? Enter / PF3 / PF7 / PF8

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction List screen and has an active session with a valid communication area
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any function key other than Enter, PF3, PF7, or PF8
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system identifies the key press as unrecognized and does not perform any transaction retrieval, navigation, or selection processing

rules.rule_name: Set Error Indicator on Invalid Key Press
rules.rule_description: When an unrecognized function key is pressed, the system must activate the error indicator flag to signal that an error condition exists, which will control subsequent screen display behavior.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Error Indicator

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction List screen and has pressed an unrecognized function key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the pressed key and determines it does not match Enter, PF3, PF7, or PF8
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error indicator flag to 'Y' (active error state) to mark that an invalid key error condition has occurred

rules.rule_name: Assign Invalid Key Error Message
rules.rule_description: When an unrecognized function key is pressed, the system must populate the screen error message area with the standard invalid key message to inform the user that their key press was not recognized.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Error Message: Invalid Key

acceptance_criteria.Given: The error indicator has been set to active due to an unrecognized function key press on the Transaction List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to re-display the Transaction List screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system populates the error message field with the standard invalid key message (sourced from the application message constant CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) to be shown to the user on the screen

rules.rule_name: Re-Display Transaction List Screen with Invalid Key Error
rules.rule_description: After detecting an invalid key press and setting the error message, the system must re-display the Transaction List screen showing the error message to the user, preserving the current screen content so the user can take a valid action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Re-Display Current Transaction List Screen with Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The error indicator is active and the invalid key error message has been set, and the screen erase flag is set to YES (default initial state)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs the send transaction list screen operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the Transaction List screen (map COTRN0A from mapset COTRN00) with the invalid key error message visible in the error message area, with the cursor positioned on the Transaction ID input field, and the screen is refreshed with an erase so the user can see the error and retry with a valid key

key_functionalities.title: Return to Previous Screen
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Return to Previous Screen Triggered])
    B{Is Target Program\nName Blank?}
    C[Default Target to\nSign-On Screen\nCOSGN00C]
    D[Record Current\nTransaction ID\nin Session Data]
    E[Record Current\nProgram Name\nin Session Data]
    F[Reset Program\nContext to Zero]
    G{Which Target\nProgram?}
    H([Transfer to\nSign-On Screen\nCOSGN00C])
    I([Transfer to\nMain Menu Screen\nCOMEN01C])

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - No Target Set| C
    B -->|No - Target Already Set| D
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    G -->|No Active Session\nor Default| H
    G -->|User Pressed PF3\nReturn to Menu| I

rules.rule_name: Default Navigation Target to Sign-On Screen When No Target Is Set
rules.rule_description: When the return-to-previous-screen process is triggered but no target program has been specified in the session, the system defaults the navigation destination to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) to ensure the user is always directed to a valid screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Default Target to Sign-On Screen COSGN00C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Return to Previous Screen process has been triggered AND the target program name stored in the session communication area (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is either blank (SPACES) or contains no value (LOW-VALUES)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the target program name before transferring control
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the target program name to 'COSGN00C' (Sign-On Screen) as the default navigation destination, overriding the blank or null value

rules.rule_name: Record Current Transaction ID in Session Data Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to any previous screen, the system captures and stores the current transaction identifier into the session communication area so the receiving program knows which transaction initiated the navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Current Transaction ID in Session Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Return to Previous Screen process has been triggered AND the target program name has been confirmed (either defaulted to COSGN00C or already set to COMEN01C)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the session communication area for the screen transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must record the current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) into the session communication area field CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, preserving the originating transaction context for the receiving program

rules.rule_name: Record Current Program Name in Session Data Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to any previous screen, the system captures and stores the current program name into the session communication area so the receiving program knows which program initiated the navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Current Program Name in Session Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Return to Previous Screen process has been triggered AND the current Transaction ID has already been recorded in the session communication area (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system continues preparing the session communication area for the screen transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must record the current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME) into the session communication area field CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, preserving the originating program identity for the receiving program

rules.rule_name: Reset Program Context to Zero Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to any previous screen, the system resets the program context indicator to zero in the session communication area, ensuring the receiving program starts without any inherited operational context from the current program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset Program Context to Zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Return to Previous Screen process has been triggered AND both the current Transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) and Program Name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) have been recorded in the session communication area
acceptance_criteria.When: The system finalizes the session communication area before the screen transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the program context value (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) to zero (0), clearing any prior operational context so the target program initializes in a clean state

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Sign-On Screen When No Active Session or Default Navigation
rules.rule_description: When the user has no active session (first-time entry with no communication area) or when the navigation target defaults to the Sign-On screen, the system transfers full control to the Sign-On program (COSGN00C), passing the complete session communication area.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer to Sign-On Screen COSGN00C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Return to Previous Screen process has been triggered AND the target program is determined to be 'COSGN00C' — either because EIBCALEN equals zero (no active session exists) OR because the target program name was blank/null and defaulted to COSGN00C AND the session communication area has been updated with the current Transaction ID, Program Name, and Program Context reset to zero
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the navigation transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must transfer full control to the Sign-On screen program 'COSGN00C', passing the complete session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), and the current program must terminate its execution

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Main Menu Screen When User Presses PF3
rules.rule_description: When the user explicitly presses PF3 to return to the main menu, the system transfers full control to the Main Menu program (COMEN01C), passing the complete session communication area.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer to Main Menu Screen COMEN01C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction List screen AND the user has pressed PF3 (Return to Menu key) AND the target program has been set to 'COMEN01C' in the session communication area AND the session communication area has been updated with the current Transaction ID, Program Name, and Program Context reset to zero
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the navigation transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must transfer full control to the Main Menu screen program 'COMEN01C', passing the complete session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), and the current program must terminate its execution

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction List program is invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins execution
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error flag is set to OFF, the end-of-file indicator is set to NOT-EOF, the next-page indicator is set to YES, the screen erase flag is set to YES (full screen refresh), the message area is cleared to spaces, the error message output field (ERRMSGO) is cleared to spaces, and the cursor is positioned on the Transaction ID input field (TRNIDINL)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Initialization
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the start of every program execution, the system resets all processing flags, clears any existing messages, and sets default display and navigation states to ensure a clean starting condition.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction List program is invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No communication area exists from a prior screen (session length equals zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) and transfers control to that screen, ending the current program execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Session Validation – No Active Session Redirect
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user attempts to access the Transaction List screen without an active session context, the system redirects them to the Sign-On screen to establish a valid session before proceeding.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An active session exists (communication area is present) and the program has not been previously re-entered
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program detects it is the first entry (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is FALSE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program marks itself as re-entered (sets CDEMO-PGM-REENTER to TRUE), clears the screen output area (COTRN0AO) to LOW-VALUES, then immediately performs forward page data loading to retrieve and display the first page of transactions

all_rules.Rule_Name: First-Time Screen Display Initialization
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user navigates to the Transaction List screen for the first time within an active session, the system initializes the screen layout and automatically loads the first page of transactions without requiring any user input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Transaction data has been loaded and the screen output area (COTRN0AO) is populated with transaction rows, header information, and any error or informational messages
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is ready to display the Transaction List screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the screen erase flag is YES, the screen (map COTRN0A from mapset COTRN00) is sent with a full ERASE and cursor positioning; if the screen erase flag is NO, the screen is sent with cursor positioning only (no erase), preserving existing screen content

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction List Screen Rendering
all_rules.Rule_Description: The transaction list screen is rendered to the user with all populated transaction data, header information, and any applicable messages. The screen can be sent with a full erase or a partial refresh depending on the navigation context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is about to send the Transaction List screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header population routine is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and time, populates the screen header with: Application Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) into TITLE01O, Application Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) into TITLE02O, the current transaction name (WS-TRANID) into TRNNAMEO, the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) into PGMNAMEO, the current date formatted as MM/DD/YY into CURDATEO, and the current time formatted as HH:MM:SS into CURTIMEO

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Header Population
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the Transaction List screen, the system populates the screen header with current date, current time, application titles, transaction name, and program name to provide context to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction List screen has been displayed to the user and the program has been previously re-entered (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits input by pressing any function key or the ENTER key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system receives the screen input from map COTRN0A (mapset COTRN00) into the input area COTRN0AI, capturing all field values including selection flags (SEL0001I–SEL0010I), transaction IDs (TRNID01I–TRNID10I), and the Transaction ID search field (TRNIDINI)

all_rules.Rule_Name: User Input Reception
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user has already been presented with the Transaction List screen and interacts with it, the system receives and captures all user input from the screen before processing any actions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted input on the Transaction List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the key pressed (EIBAID)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If ENTER was pressed, the system performs transaction selection and search processing; if PF3 was pressed, the system navigates to the Main Menu (COMEN01C); if PF7 was pressed, the system performs backward page navigation; if PF8 was pressed, the system performs forward page navigation; if any other key was pressed, the system displays an invalid key error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Function Key Routing
all_rules.Rule_Description: After receiving user input, the system routes processing to the appropriate business function based on which key the user pressed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the Transaction List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the selection fields for all 10 displayed transaction rows (SEL0001I through SEL0010I)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system checks each selection field in order from row 1 to row 10; the first row whose selection field is not spaces and not LOW-VALUES is treated as the selected row — its selection flag value is stored in CDEMO-CT00-TRN-SEL-FLG and its corresponding Transaction ID (TRNID01I through TRNID10I) is stored in CDEMO-CT00-TRN-SELECTED; if no selection field contains a value, both CDEMO-CT00-TRN-SEL-FLG and CDEMO-CT00-TRN-SELECTED are set to spaces

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Row Selection Detection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses ENTER, the system scans all 10 transaction rows on the screen to detect which row, if any, the user has selected by entering a value in the selection field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered 'S' or 's' in a selection field next to a transaction row and the corresponding Transaction ID is not blank or LOW-VALUES
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system validates the selection flag value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to COTRN01C (Transaction Detail screen), records the current transaction name (WS-TRANID) in CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, records the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) in CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, sets the program context to 0, and transfers control to COTRN01C passing the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Detail Navigation on Valid Selection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects a transaction using the valid selection code 'S', the system transfers control to the Transaction Detail screen, passing the selected transaction's ID for detailed viewing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a value in a selection field (CDEMO-CT00-TRN-SEL-FLG is not spaces and not LOW-VALUES) and the corresponding Transaction ID (CDEMO-CT00-TRN-SELECTED) is not blank or LOW-VALUES
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The selection flag value is not 'S' and not 's'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the error message 'Invalid selection. Valid value is S' in the message area (WS-MESSAGE) and positions the cursor on the Transaction ID input field (TRNIDINL set to -1); the user remains on the Transaction List screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid Transaction Selection Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters a value other than 'S' or 's' in a transaction selection field, the system rejects the selection and displays an error message indicating the only valid selection value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the Transaction List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction ID search input field (TRNIDINI) is blank (spaces) or LOW-VALUES
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the internal transaction search key (TRAN-ID) to LOW-VALUES, which causes the file browse to start from the beginning of the transaction file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction ID Search Input – Blank Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user leaves the Transaction ID search field blank, the system interprets this as a request to start the transaction list from the very beginning of the transaction file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the Transaction List screen and the Transaction ID search field (TRNIDINI) contains a non-blank, non-LOW-VALUES value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The value entered in TRNIDINI is not numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG) to 'Y', displays the error message 'Tran ID must be Numeric ...' in the message area (WS-MESSAGE), positions the cursor on the Transaction ID input field (TRNIDINL set to -1), and immediately sends the Transaction List screen to the user without performing any file browse

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction ID Search Input – Non-Numeric Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction ID search field only accepts numeric values. If the user enters a non-numeric value, the system rejects the input and displays an appropriate error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the Transaction List screen and the Transaction ID search field (TRNIDINI) contains a non-blank value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The value entered in TRNIDINI is numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system moves the entered value from TRNIDINI into the internal transaction search key (TRAN-ID), which is then used as the starting position for the forward file browse

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction ID Search Input – Valid Numeric Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user enters a valid numeric Transaction ID in the search field, the system uses it as the starting point for browsing the transaction file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF8 on the Transaction List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether a next page of transactions is available (NEXT-PAGE-YES indicator)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the next-page indicator is YES, the system uses the last Transaction ID displayed on the current page (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST) as the starting browse key — if CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST is blank or LOW-VALUES, HIGH-VALUES is used instead — and performs forward page data loading; if the next-page indicator is NO, the system displays the message 'You are already at the bottom of the page...' and re-displays the current screen without loading new data (SEND-ERASE set to NO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Forward Page Navigation – PF8 Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF8 to scroll forward, the system determines whether a next page of transactions is available before attempting to load it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF7 on the Transaction List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the PF7 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the next-page indicator to YES, then uses the first Transaction ID displayed on the current page (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST) as the starting browse key — if CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST is blank or LOW-VALUES, LOW-VALUES is used instead — and positions the cursor on the Transaction ID input field (TRNIDINL set to -1)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Backward Page Navigation – PF7 Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF7 to scroll backward, the system sets up the navigation context using the first transaction on the current page as the reference point before checking page boundary conditions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF7 on the Transaction List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the current page number (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current page number is greater than 1, the system proceeds with backward page data loading; if the current page number is 1 or less, the system displays the message 'You are already at the top of the page...' sets the screen erase flag to NO, and re-displays the current screen without loading new data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Top-of-List Boundary Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before scrolling backward, the system checks whether the user is already on the first page to prevent navigating beyond the beginning of the transaction list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF8 on the Transaction List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the next-page availability indicator (NEXT-PAGE-YES/NO)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the next-page indicator is YES (more transactions exist beyond the current page), the system proceeds with forward page data loading; if the next-page indicator is NO, the system displays the message 'You are already at the bottom of the page...' sets the screen erase flag to NO, and re-displays the current screen without loading new data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Bottom-of-List Boundary Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before scrolling forward, the system checks whether additional pages of transactions exist beyond the current page to prevent navigating beyond the end of the transaction list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A starting Transaction ID (TRAN-ID) has been established (either from user input, LOW-VALUES for start of file, or the last Transaction ID from the previous page)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs forward page data loading
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system starts a forward browse of the transaction file (TRANSACT) from TRAN-ID; if the key pressed was not ENTER, PF7, or PF3, the system reads and skips the first record (to move past the current position); the system clears all 10 display rows; then reads up to 10 transaction records sequentially, populating display rows 1 through 10 with Transaction ID, Date, Description, and Amount for each record read; the page counter (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM) is reset to 0 before loading begins (on ENTER key) and incremented by 1 after loading; the browse is then closed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Forward Page Data Loading
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system loads a page of up to 10 transactions by browsing forward through the transaction file starting from a specified Transaction ID, populating the display rows sequentially.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The first Transaction ID of the current page (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST) has been set as the browse starting key (TRAN-ID) and the current page number is greater than 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs backward page data loading
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system starts a backward browse of the transaction file (TRANSACT) from TRAN-ID; if the key pressed was not ENTER or PF8, the system reads and skips the first previous record; the system clears all 10 display rows; then reads up to 10 transaction records in reverse order, populating display rows 10 down to 1 with Transaction ID, Date, Description, and Amount; after filling the rows, the system attempts to read one more previous record — if successful and the page number is greater than 1, the page number is decremented by 1; otherwise the page number is set to 1; the browse is then closed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Backward Page Data Loading
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system loads a page of up to 10 transactions by browsing backward through the transaction file starting from the first Transaction ID of the current page, filling display rows from bottom to top.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A page load operation (forward or backward) is about to begin populating transaction display rows
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initializes the transaction display data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each of the 10 display rows (rows 1 through 10), the system sets the Transaction ID field (TRNID01I–TRNID10I), Transaction Date field (TDATE01I–TDATE10I), Transaction Description field (TDESC01I–TDESC10I), and Transaction Amount field (TAMT001I–TAMT010I) to spaces

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Display Row Initialization
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the transaction list with new data, the system clears all 10 display rows to ensure no stale data from a previous page is shown to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been successfully read from the TRANSACT file and the current row index (WS-IDX) is between 1 and 10
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the transaction data for the current row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Based on the row index (WS-IDX 1 through 10), the system places the Transaction ID (TRAN-ID) into the corresponding TRNID field (TRNID01I–TRNID10I), the formatted transaction date (WS-TRAN-DATE in MM/DD/YY format) into the corresponding TDATE field (TDATE01I–TDATE10I), the Transaction Description (TRAN-DESC) into the corresponding TDESC field (TDESC01I–TDESC10I), and the formatted Transaction Amount (WS-TRAN-AMT) into the corresponding TAMT field (TAMT001I–TAMT010I)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Record Population into Display Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each transaction record read from the file, the system formats and places the transaction data into the correct display row on the screen based on the current row index.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read from the TRANSACT file containing a full timestamp in TRAN-ORIG-TS
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the transaction date for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system extracts the year (positions 3–4 of the date portion of WS-TIMESTAMP-DT-YYYY) into WS-CURDATE-YY, the month (WS-TIMESTAMP-DT-MM) into WS-CURDATE-MM, and the day (WS-TIMESTAMP-DT-DD) into WS-CURDATE-DD, then combines them into the MM/DD/YY format (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) stored in WS-TRAN-DATE for display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Date Formatting
all_rules.Rule_Description: Transaction dates stored as full timestamps in the system are reformatted into a user-friendly MM/DD/YY display format before being shown on the transaction list screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read from the TRANSACT file containing a raw transaction amount in TRAN-AMT
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the transaction amount for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system moves the raw transaction amount (TRAN-AMT) into the formatted display amount field (WS-TRAN-AMT), which applies the defined picture clause formatting for display on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Amount Formatting
all_rules.Rule_Description: Transaction amounts retrieved from the file are formatted into a display-ready format before being shown on the transaction list screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Transaction records are being populated into the display rows during a page load operation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates row 1 (WS-IDX = 1) and row 10 (WS-IDX = 10)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: When populating row 1, the Transaction ID (TRAN-ID) is stored in both TRNID01I of COTRN0AI and CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST; when populating row 10, the Transaction ID (TRAN-ID) is stored in both TRNID10I of COTRN0AI and CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST

all_rules.Rule_Name: First and Last Transaction ID Tracking for Pagination
all_rules.Rule_Description: As transactions are loaded onto the display page, the system records the Transaction IDs of the first and last records shown. These are used as reference points for subsequent forward and backward page navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully populated all 10 display rows with transaction data during a forward page load
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to read one additional record beyond the 10th displayed record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the additional record is successfully read (TRANSACT-NOT-EOF and no error), the next-page indicator is set to YES (PF8 navigation is enabled); if no additional record exists (end of file reached), the next-page indicator is set to NO (PF8 navigation is disabled); if fewer than 10 records were loaded (WS-IDX did not reach 11), the next-page indicator is also set to NO

all_rules.Rule_Name: Next Page Availability Detection
all_rules.Rule_Description: After loading 10 transaction records onto the current page, the system attempts to read one additional record to determine whether more transactions exist beyond the current page, enabling or disabling the forward navigation (PF8) capability.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A page load operation (forward or backward) has completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system updates the page number counter (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For forward navigation: if records were loaded (WS-IDX > 1) or all 10 rows were filled, the page number is incremented by 1; the updated page number is displayed in PAGENUMI of COTRN0AI; for backward navigation: if more previous records exist and the current page number is greater than 1, the page number is decremented by 1; if no more previous records exist or the page number is already 1, the page number is set to 1; the updated page number is displayed in PAGENUMI of COTRN0AI

all_rules.Rule_Name: Page Number Tracking – Increment and Decrement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system maintains an accurate page number counter that increments when navigating forward and decrements when navigating backward, always reflecting the current page position within the transaction list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF3
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to COMEN01C (Main Menu) and transfers control to that program passing the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), ending the Transaction List program execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return to Main Menu – PF3 Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3, the system exits the Transaction List screen and returns the user to the Main Menu screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any key other than ENTER, PF3, PF7, or PF8
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG) to 'Y', positions the cursor on the Transaction ID input field (TRNIDINL set to -1), displays the standard invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) in the message area (WS-MESSAGE), and re-displays the Transaction List screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid Key Error Handling
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses a key that is not supported on the Transaction List screen, the system displays an error message informing the user that the key pressed is not valid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is performing a return-to-previous-screen operation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is LOW-VALUES or spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to COSGN00C (Sign-On screen), records the current transaction name (WS-TRANID) in CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, records the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) in CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, sets the program context to zeros, and transfers control to the destination program passing the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return to Previous Screen – Default Sign-On Fallback
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system needs to return to a previous screen and no specific destination program has been defined, it defaults to the Sign-On screen to ensure the user is always directed to a valid screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction List program begins a new execution cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error flag must be set to OFF, indicating no error condition exists at the start of processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Error Flag at Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the beginning of each program execution cycle, the error flag must be turned off to ensure no residual error state from a previous interaction affects the current processing cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction List program begins a new execution cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction file status must be set to 'Not End-of-File', indicating the file is ready for reading and no prior end-of-file condition is active

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Transaction File Read Status at Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the beginning of each program execution cycle, the transaction file read status must be set to 'Not End-of-File' to ensure the system is ready to read transaction records and no prior end-of-file condition carries over.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction List program begins a new execution cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next-page indicator must be set to 'No Next Page', ensuring that forward pagination availability is freshly determined during the current cycle rather than inherited from a previous interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Next Page Availability Indicator at Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the beginning of each program execution cycle, the next-page availability indicator must be reset to indicate that no next page is confirmed available, preventing stale pagination state from a prior interaction from influencing current navigation behavior.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction List program begins a new execution cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen display mode must be set to 'Full Erase', ensuring the transaction list screen will be fully refreshed and cleared when displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Screen Display Mode to Full Erase at Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the beginning of each program execution cycle, the screen display mode must be set to 'Full Erase', so that when the transaction list screen is sent to the user, the entire screen is refreshed and cleared of any previous content.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction List program begins a new execution cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error message field in working storage (WS-MESSAGE) must be set to spaces, removing any error message text that may have been set during a previous interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Working Storage Error Message at Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the beginning of each program execution cycle, the error message held in working storage must be cleared to spaces, ensuring no residual error message text from a prior interaction is inadvertently carried forward and displayed to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction List program begins a new execution cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error message field in the screen output display area (ERRMSGO of COTRN0AO) must be set to spaces, so no prior error message is visible on the transaction list screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Screen Display Area Error Message at Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the beginning of each program execution cycle, the error message field in the screen output area must be cleared to spaces, ensuring the transaction list screen does not display any stale error message from a prior interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction List program begins a new execution cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor position must be set to the Transaction ID input field (TRNIDINL of COTRN0AI) by assigning it a value of -1, so that when the screen is displayed, the cursor automatically lands on the Transaction ID entry field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Default Cursor Position to Transaction ID Field at Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the beginning of each program execution cycle, the screen cursor must be defaulted to the Transaction ID input field, guiding the user to the primary search entry point on the transaction list screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the Transaction List screen and no active session context is present (communication area length is zero, indicating a new or expired session)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether a valid user session exists
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system determines that no valid session is present and sets the destination screen to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) to force user authentication before proceeding

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Missing User Session and Initiate Sign-On Redirect
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user attempts to access the Transaction List screen without an active session context, the system detects the absence of a session and initiates a redirect to the Sign-On screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to redirect the user to a previous or designated screen and the destination program field (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) contains low-values or spaces, meaning no destination has been explicitly set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether a destination screen has been defined prior to executing the redirect
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system defaults the destination to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C), ensuring the user is redirected to a valid and secure entry point

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Default Destination to Sign-On Screen When No Destination Is Defined
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before redirecting the user, the system verifies that a destination screen has been explicitly set. If no destination has been defined, the system defaults the destination to the Sign-On screen to ensure the user is always directed to a valid screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined the destination screen and is preparing to redirect the user away from the Transaction List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the redirect preparation steps
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the current transaction identifier (WS-TRANID) as the originating transaction (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), records the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) as the originating program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), and sets the program context indicator to zero (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT = 0) in the session communication area before transferring control

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Program and Transaction Details Before Redirect
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring the user to another screen, the system captures and records the current program name and transaction identifier in the session communication area. This preserves the originating context so the destination screen knows where the user came from.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination screen has been set (either explicitly to COSGN00C or defaulted to COSGN00C) and the current program and transaction details have been recorded in the session communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the screen transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system transfers full control to the Sign-On screen program (COSGN00C), passing the complete session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), and the Transaction List screen program terminates its current execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redirect User to Sign-On Screen by Transferring Program Control
all_rules.Rule_Description: After recording the originating context and confirming the destination, the system transfers full program control to the Sign-On screen, passing the current session communication area so the destination screen has access to all relevant session data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the Transaction List screen and a valid active session context exists (communication area length is greater than zero, indicating an established session)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether a valid user session is present
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system grants access, loads the session communication area data (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) from the passed context, and proceeds to display the Transaction List screen to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Allow Access to Transaction List Screen for Users with Valid Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user accesses the Transaction List screen and a valid active session context is present, the system allows the user to proceed and loads the session data to support the transaction listing functionality.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has an active session with a valid communication area (EIBCALEN > 0) and the program has not been previously re-entered (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER flag is not set to TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction List program (COTRN0AC) is invoked for the first time in the current session
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies this as a first-time entry and proceeds to initialize the screen, load the first page of transactions, and display the transaction list to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect and Handle First-Time Program Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters the Transaction List screen for the first time within an active session, the system detects this as a first-time entry and initiates the full screen initialization and data load sequence.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has detected a first-time entry to the Transaction List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The first-time initialization sequence begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The session re-entry flag (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) is set to TRUE, ensuring all future interactions with this screen in the same session are treated as returning visits and not re-initialized

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Session as Re-entrant for Subsequent Visits
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon first-time entry, the system immediately marks the session as re-entrant so that on all subsequent interactions (key presses, navigation), the program follows the returning-user flow instead of the first-time initialization flow.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has detected a first-time entry to the Transaction List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen initialization sequence is triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All output display fields on the Transaction List screen (COTRN0AO) are cleared to LOW-VALUES, removing any previously displayed data or residual values

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Screen Layout on First Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: On first-time entry to the Transaction List screen, all screen output fields are reset to empty (LOW-VALUES) to ensure no residual or stale data is displayed before the fresh transaction data is loaded.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction List screen is being loaded for the first time and the Transaction ID input field (TRNIDINI) is blank or contains only spaces or low-values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to retrieve transactions from the transaction file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction search key (TRAN-ID) is set to LOW-VALUES, directing the file browse to start from the very first record in the transaction file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Transaction Search Starting Point to Beginning of File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no Transaction ID is provided in the search field (field is blank or empty), the system sets the search key to the lowest possible value so that browsing begins from the very first transaction record available.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is about to load the first page of transactions on first-time entry
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The page forward process is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM) is set to zero (0) so that after loading the first page, the page counter will be incremented to 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Page Number to Zero Before Loading First Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before loading the first page of transactions, the page counter is reset to zero so that after the first page is successfully loaded, the page number correctly increments to 1.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is about to populate the transaction list screen with a new set of transaction records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The page loading process begins and no errors have been encountered during the file browse start
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All 10 transaction display rows on the screen are cleared to spaces — each row's Transaction ID, Transaction Date, Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount fields are set to spaces before new data is loaded

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All 10 Transaction Display Rows Before Populating
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the transaction list with fresh data, all 10 transaction display rows on the screen are cleared to spaces to prevent any stale or partial data from a previous page being shown alongside new records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction search key (TRAN-ID) has been set to LOW-VALUES (beginning of file) and the system is ready to retrieve transaction records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction file browse is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system opens a browse session on the transaction file (TRANSACT) starting at the position identified by the TRAN-ID key, allowing sequential reading of records from that position forward

all_rules.Rule_Name: Start Browsing Transactions from the Specified Starting Position
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system initiates a sequential browse of the transaction file starting from the specified Transaction ID key position, enabling forward or backward reading of transaction records from that point.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A browse session on the transaction file is active and the system is in the process of loading transaction records for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system requests the next transaction record from the file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next sequential transaction record is retrieved from the transaction file into the transaction record buffer (TRAN-RECORD), making its Transaction ID, Transaction Date, Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount available for display; if no more records exist, the end-of-file condition is set

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Next Transaction Record Sequentially
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system reads the next available transaction record sequentially from the transaction file during the page-loading process, retrieving one record at a time to populate the screen display rows.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is in the process of loading transaction records for the current page and the transaction file browse is active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Each transaction record is read from the file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the next available screen row (rows 1 through 10) with the transaction data; the loading loop continues until the row index (WS-IDX) reaches 11 (10 records loaded), or the end of the transaction file is reached (TRANSACT-EOF), or an error condition is raised — whichever occurs first

all_rules.Rule_Name: Load Up to Maximum 10 Transaction Records Per Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: The transaction list page displays a maximum of 10 transactions. The system continues reading and populating transaction rows until either 10 records have been loaded, the end of the transaction file is reached, or an error occurs.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been successfully read from the transaction file and contains an original transaction timestamp (TRAN-ORIG-TS)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction data is being prepared for display on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction's original timestamp (TRAN-ORIG-TS) is parsed to extract the year (2-digit: positions 3-4 of the year component), month (WS-TIMESTAMP-DT-MM), and day (WS-TIMESTAMP-DT-DD), and these are assembled into MM/DD/YY format (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) stored in WS-TRAN-DATE for display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Transaction Date to MM/DD/YY Display Format
all_rules.Rule_Description: The transaction's original timestamp stored in the system is reformatted into a user-friendly MM/DD/YY date format before being displayed on the transaction list screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been successfully read from the transaction file and contains a transaction amount (TRAN-AMT)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction data is being prepared for display on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction amount (TRAN-AMT) is moved into the display-formatted working storage field (WS-TRAN-AMT) which applies the appropriate sign and decimal formatting for presentation on the transaction list screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Transaction Amount for Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: The raw transaction amount from the transaction record is formatted into a display-ready value with appropriate sign and decimal representation before being placed on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read and its date and amount have been formatted, and the current row index (WS-IDX) is between 1 and 10
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction data is placed into the screen display fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Based on the current row index (WS-IDX), the system populates the corresponding screen row fields: Transaction ID (TRNIDxxI), Transaction Date (TDATExxI), Transaction Description (TDESCxxI), and Transaction Amount (TAMTxxxI) where xx/xxx corresponds to the row number (01 through 10)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Row with Transaction Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each retrieved transaction record's details — Transaction ID, formatted date, description, and formatted amount — are placed into the corresponding numbered screen row (1 through 10) on the transaction list display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Transaction records are being loaded into the screen display rows and the current row index (WS-IDX) is 1 (first row)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The first transaction record is placed into screen row 1
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID of the first record (TRAN-ID) is saved into the first-transaction-on-page tracker (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST), which will be used as the reference point for backward page navigation (PF7)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Track First Transaction ID on Page for Backward Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction ID of the first record displayed on the current page is saved so that when the user navigates backward (PF7), the system knows the correct starting position to retrieve the previous page of transactions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Transaction records are being loaded into the screen display rows and the current row index (WS-IDX) is 10 (last row)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The tenth transaction record is placed into screen row 10
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID of the last record (TRAN-ID) is saved into the last-transaction-on-page tracker (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST), which will be used as the reference point for forward page navigation (PF8)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Track Last Transaction ID on Page for Forward Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction ID of the last record displayed on the current page is saved so that when the user navigates forward (PF8), the system knows the correct starting position to retrieve the next page of transactions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully loaded 10 transaction records into the screen display rows and no errors have occurred (ERR-FLG-OFF) and end-of-file has not been reached (TRANSACT-NOT-EOF)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to read one additional transaction record beyond the 10 already loaded
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system performs one more READNEXT on the transaction file to check if any records exist beyond the current page; the result of this read determines whether the next-page indicator is set to YES or NO

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read One Additional Record to Determine If Next Page Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: After loading 10 transaction records for the current page, the system attempts to read one more record from the file solely to determine whether additional transactions exist beyond the current page, which controls whether PF8 (next page) navigation is available to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has loaded 10 transaction records and performed a look-ahead read to check for additional records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The look-ahead read successfully retrieves a record (TRANSACT-NOT-EOF is true and ERR-FLG-OFF is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next-page availability flag (NEXT-PAGE) is set to YES, enabling the user to navigate forward to the next page using PF8

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enable Next Page Navigation When More Records Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the look-ahead read confirms that more transaction records exist beyond the current page, the system enables forward navigation (PF8) so the user can proceed to the next page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to load transaction records for the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Either the look-ahead read finds no more records (TRANSACT-EOF condition is reached) OR fewer than 10 records were loaded (WS-IDX did not reach 11)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next-page availability flag (NEXT-PAGE) is set to NO, disabling PF8 forward navigation; if at least one record was loaded (WS-IDX > 1), the page number is still incremented

all_rules.Rule_Name: Disable Next Page Navigation When No More Records Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the look-ahead read confirms that no more transaction records exist beyond the current page, or if fewer than 10 records were loaded, the system disables forward navigation (PF8) to prevent the user from attempting to navigate to a non-existent next page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The page counter (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM) was set to zero before loading began and at least one transaction record was successfully loaded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The page loading process completes (either 10 records loaded or end of file reached)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The page counter (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by 1 (from 0 to 1) and this page number is moved to the screen page number display field (PAGENUMI of COTRN0AI) so the user sees 'Page 1'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Page Number to 1 After Loading First Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully loading the first page of transactions (starting from page counter zero), the page number is incremented to 1 and displayed on the screen so the user knows they are viewing page 1 of the transaction list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction list screen is about to be sent to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header population routine (POPULATE-HEADER-INFO) is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen header is populated with: Application Title line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01 → TITLE01O), Application Title line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02 → TITLE02O), current transaction name (WS-TRANID → TRNNAMEO), current program name (WS-PGMNAME → PGMNAMEO), current system date formatted as MM/DD/YY (CURDATEO), and current system time formatted as HH:MM:SS (CURTIMEO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Header with Current Date, Time, and Program Information
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the transaction list screen, the system populates the screen header area with the application titles, current system date, current system time, the transaction name, and the program name to provide context to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All transaction data rows and screen header fields have been populated and the SEND-ERASE flag is set to YES (as initialized at program start)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction list screen is sent to the user's terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen map COTRN0A from mapset COTRN00 is sent to the terminal using the COTRN0AO output data, with ERASE option to clear the entire terminal screen before displaying, and with CURSOR positioning active; any error or informational message (WS-MESSAGE) is displayed in the message field (ERRMSGO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Transaction List Screen to User with Full Erase
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all transaction data and header information have been prepared, the complete transaction list screen is sent to the user's terminal, fully erasing any previous screen content and positioning the cursor at the Transaction ID input field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is about to display the Transaction List screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header population process is triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and current system time from the operating environment and stores them for use in the screen header fields

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time for Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the transaction list screen, the system retrieves the current system date and time to populate the screen header, ensuring users always see accurate temporal context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating the Transaction List screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The application title fields are being set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Title Line 1 (TITLE01O) is populated from the application common data area field CCDA-TITLE01, and Title Line 2 (TITLE02O) is populated from the application common data area field CCDA-TITLE02, and both title lines are displayed in the screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Application Title Lines on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The transaction list screen header must display two standardized application title lines sourced from the application's common data area, ensuring consistent branding across all screens.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system date has been retrieved and the screen header is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The date is formatted for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The month component is extracted into MM, the day component is extracted into DD, the last two digits of the year are extracted into YY, and the formatted date in MM/DD/YY format is placed into the screen header date field (CURDATEO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Display Current Date in MM/DD/YY Format
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current date displayed in the screen header must be formatted as MM/DD/YY, extracting the month, day, and two-digit year components from the system date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system time has been retrieved and the screen header is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The time is formatted for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The hours component is extracted into HH, the minutes component is extracted into MM, the seconds component is extracted into SS, and the formatted time in HH:MM:SS format is placed into the screen header time field (CURTIMEO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Display Current Time in HH:MM:SS Format
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current time displayed in the screen header must be formatted as HH:MM:SS, extracting the hours, minutes, and seconds components from the system time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating the Transaction List screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction identifier field is being set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is moved to the transaction name field (TRNNAMEO) in the screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Current Transaction ID on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The screen header must display the current transaction identifier (the CICS transaction ID under which this program is running) to provide users with context about which transaction they are operating in.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating the Transaction List screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program name field is being set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is moved to the program name field (PGMNAMEO) in the screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Current Program Name on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The screen header must display the name of the currently executing program to provide users and support staff with context about which program is being used.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed processing and is preparing to display the Transaction List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen message area is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current working storage message (WS-MESSAGE) — which may contain an error message such as 'Tran ID must be Numeric...', 'Invalid selection. Valid value is S', 'You are already at the top of the page...', 'You are already at the bottom of the page...', 'You have reached the bottom of the page...', 'You have reached the top of the page...', or 'Unable to lookup transaction...' — is moved to the screen error message output field (ERRMSGO of COTRN0AO) for display to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Error or Informational Message in Screen Message Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: Any error or informational message generated during processing must be displayed to the user in the designated message area of the Transaction List screen before the screen is sent.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is ready to send the Transaction List screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen send mode is evaluated using the SEND-ERASE flag
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the SEND-ERASE flag is set to YES (indicating a fresh page load, new search, or initial display), the screen is sent with a full screen erase (ERASE option) and cursor positioning; if the SEND-ERASE flag is set to NO (indicating a boundary condition message such as already at top or bottom of page, or an error redisplay), the screen is sent without erasing existing data (partial refresh) but with cursor positioning

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Screen Send Mode: Full Refresh vs Partial Refresh
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must determine whether to send the transaction list screen with a full screen erase (fresh page load) or a partial refresh (preserving existing screen data), based on the nature of the current display event.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SEND-ERASE flag is set to YES, indicating a fresh page load or initial display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction List screen (COTRN0A from mapset COTRN00) is sent to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is sent with the ERASE option, which clears the entire screen before displaying the new transaction list data, and the cursor is positioned at the Transaction ID input field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Transaction List Screen with Full Screen Refresh
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new page of transactions is being displayed for the first time or after a new search, the transaction list screen is sent to the user with a complete screen refresh, clearing any previously displayed data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SEND-ERASE flag is set to NO, indicating a boundary condition or error redisplay where existing screen data should be preserved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction List screen (COTRN0A from mapset COTRN00) is sent to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is sent without the ERASE option, preserving the existing transaction list data already displayed on screen, and the cursor is positioned at the Transaction ID input field; this occurs in scenarios such as when the user is already at the top of the page (PF7 at page 1) or already at the bottom of the page (PF8 at last page)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Transaction List Screen with Partial Refresh
all_rules.Rule_Description: When displaying a boundary message (e.g., already at top or bottom of page) or an error message without changing the underlying transaction data, the screen is refreshed partially to preserve the existing transaction list data already visible to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction List program begins a new execution cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its processing flags
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The SEND-ERASE flag is set to YES (SEND-ERASE-YES) by default, so that the screen will be sent with a full erase unless a boundary message condition (already at top or bottom) overrides it to NO during PF7 or PF8 processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Screen Erase Mode to Full Refresh at Program Initialization
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the start of every program execution cycle, the screen send mode is defaulted to full refresh (ERASE), ensuring that any new transaction list display starts with a clean screen unless explicitly overridden by a boundary or error condition.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process has been initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins preparing the Transaction List screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and time, storing the full date-time value including year, month, day, hours, minutes, and seconds for subsequent formatting and display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time for Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the screen header, the system must retrieve the current system date and time to ensure the header reflects real-time information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress and the current system date and time have been retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the screen header fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The application title line 1 value from the central application configuration (CCDA-TITLE01) is placed into the Title Line 1 field (TITLE01O) of the Transaction List screen output map (COTRN0AO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Place Application Title Line 1 onto Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The first line of the application title, sourced from the central application configuration (CCDA-TITLE01), must be displayed in the designated title area of the Transaction List screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress and Title Line 1 has been placed on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues populating the screen header fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The application title line 2 value from the central application configuration (CCDA-TITLE02) is placed into the Title Line 2 field (TITLE02O) of the Transaction List screen output map (COTRN0AO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Place Application Title Line 2 onto Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The second line of the application title, sourced from the central application configuration (CCDA-TITLE02), must be displayed in the designated title area of the Transaction List screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress and both application title lines have been placed on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues populating the screen header fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is placed into the Transaction Name field (TRNNAMEO) of the Transaction List screen output map (COTRN0AO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Place Transaction ID onto Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current transaction identifier (the CICS transaction ID under which this program is running) must be displayed in the transaction name area of the Transaction List screen header for user reference.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress and the transaction ID has been placed on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues populating the screen header fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is placed into the Program Name field (PGMNAMEO) of the Transaction List screen output map (COTRN0AO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Place Program Name onto Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The name of the currently executing program must be displayed in the program name area of the Transaction List screen header for user reference and traceability.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system date has been retrieved and the program name has been placed on the screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the current date for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system extracts the month portion (WS-CURDATE-MONTH) into the month field (WS-CURDATE-MM), extracts the day portion (WS-CURDATE-DAY) into the day field (WS-CURDATE-DD), and extracts only the last 2 digits of the year (positions 3 and 4 of WS-CURDATE-YEAR) into the 2-digit year field (WS-CURDATE-YY), resulting in a date arranged in MM/DD/YY format (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Current Date as MM/DD/YY for Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current system date must be formatted into MM/DD/YY display format by extracting the month, day, and the last two digits of the year from the full system date before being placed on the screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current date has been formatted into MM/DD/YY format (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system places the formatted date onto the screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted date in MM/DD/YY format (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) is placed into the Current Date field (CURDATEO) of the Transaction List screen output map (COTRN0AO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Place Formatted Date MM/DD/YY onto Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The formatted current date in MM/DD/YY format must be displayed in the current date field of the Transaction List screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system time has been retrieved and the formatted date has been placed on the screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the current time for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system extracts the hours portion (WS-CURTIME-HOURS) into the hours field (WS-CURTIME-HH), extracts the minutes portion (WS-CURTIME-MINUTE) into the minutes field (WS-CURTIME-MM), and extracts the seconds portion (WS-CURTIME-SECOND) into the seconds field (WS-CURTIME-SS), resulting in a time arranged in HH:MM:SS format (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Current Time as HH:MM:SS for Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current system time must be formatted into HH:MM:SS display format by extracting the hours, minutes, and seconds from the full system time before being placed on the screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current time has been formatted into HH:MM:SS format (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system places the formatted time onto the screen header
