Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The file position moves one record backward past the starting transaction ID, so the subsequent page-fill reads retrieve records from the previous page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Boundary Record Before Loading Previous Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before loading the previous page of transactions, the system reads one record backward to move past the boundary record (the first record of the current page), so that the previous page contains records that precede the current page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has initiated a browse and attempted one backward read to skip the boundary record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The backward read returns an end-of-file condition, indicating the beginning of the transaction file has been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the end-of-file indicator to TRUE, displays the message 'You have reached the top of the page...' on the Transaction List screen, and stops loading records for the previous page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Beginning of File Reached When Skipping Boundary Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the backward read to skip the boundary record reaches the beginning of the transaction file, the system notifies the user that no previous records are available.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The browse has been successfully initiated and the boundary record has been skipped without reaching the beginning of the file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to load the previous page of transactions
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All 10 transaction display rows on the screen are cleared, setting Transaction ID, Transaction Date, Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount fields to spaces for rows 1 through 10

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All Transaction Display Rows Before Loading Previous Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the screen with the previous page of transactions, all 10 transaction display rows must be cleared to blank values to ensure no stale data from the previous display remains visible.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All 10 transaction display rows have been cleared and the system is ready to populate the previous page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins the backward page population loop
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The row index is set to 10, and the system begins filling transaction data starting from the bottom row of the display, working upward toward row 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Row Index to 10 for Bottom-Up Page Population
all_rules.Rule_Description: When loading a previous page of transactions by reading backward, the screen rows are filled from the bottom (row 10) upward to row 1, so that the transactions appear in correct chronological order on screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is in the backward page population loop with a row index starting at 10
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether to continue reading backward
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system continues reading backward and populating rows only if the row index is greater than 0 AND no end-of-file condition has been reached AND no error flag has been set; the loop stops when the row index reaches 0, end-of-file is reached, or an error occurs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Continue Reading Backward While Rows Remain and Records Are Available
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system continues reading transaction records backward and populating screen rows as long as there are unfilled rows remaining on the screen and transaction records are still available in the file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward page population loop is active, the row index is greater than 0, and no end-of-file or error condition exists
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a backward read on the Transaction file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If successful, the transaction record containing Transaction ID, Transaction Date (as original timestamp), Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount is retrieved and made available for display; if end-of-file is reached, the end-of-file indicator is set to TRUE and the message 'You have reached the top of the page...' is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Next Transaction Record Backward from Transaction File
all_rules.Rule_Description: During backward page population, the system reads the next available transaction record in reverse order from the transaction file to populate the current screen row.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been successfully read from the Transaction file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the transaction date for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system extracts the year (last 2 digits), month (MM), and day (DD) from the transaction's original timestamp and formats them as MM/DD/YY for display in the transaction date field on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Transaction Date from Timestamp to MM/DD/YY Display Format
all_rules.Rule_Description: The transaction's original timestamp stored in the system must be converted to a user-friendly MM/DD/YY date format before being displayed on the transaction list screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read and the transaction date has been formatted to MM/DD/YY
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the screen row corresponding to the current row index (1 through 10)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID, formatted Transaction Date (MM/DD/YY), Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount are placed into the screen display fields for the row matching the current row index value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Row with Transaction Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each successfully read transaction record is displayed on the corresponding screen row with its Transaction ID, formatted date, description, and amount.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating transaction rows during backward page load and the current row index equals 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system places transaction data into screen row 1
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID of that record is saved as the FIRST Transaction ID of the current page (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST), to be used as the starting reference point when the user subsequently presses PF7 to go to the previous page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record First Transaction ID When Populating Row 1
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the transaction data is placed into row 1 of the screen (the topmost row), the system records that transaction's ID as the first transaction ID of the current page, which will be used as the reference point for future backward navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating transaction rows during backward page load and the current row index equals 10
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system places transaction data into screen row 10
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID of that record is saved as the LAST Transaction ID of the current page (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST), to be used as the starting reference point when the user subsequently presses PF8 to go to the next page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Last Transaction ID When Populating Row 10
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the transaction data is placed into row 10 of the screen (the bottommost row), the system records that transaction's ID as the last transaction ID of the current page, which will be used as the reference point for future forward navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been successfully read and populated into the screen row at the current row index during backward page loading
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes populating the current screen row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The row index is decremented by 1 (e.g., from 10 to 9, from 9 to 8, continuing down to 1), so the next backward read will populate the row above the current one

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decrement Row Index After Each Backward Record Population
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each transaction record is successfully read and placed into a screen row during backward page loading, the row index is decremented by 1 to move to the next row upward on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward page population loop has completed (either 10 rows are filled or end-of-file was reached) and at least one record was loaded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs one additional backward read on the Transaction file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If a record is found, it confirms that more transactions exist before the current page; if end-of-file is reached, it confirms the current page is the first page of the transaction list

all_rules.Rule_Name: Check for Previous Page Existence After Filling Current Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all available transaction records have been loaded for the current page display, the system attempts one additional backward read to determine whether a further previous page of transactions exists.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The additional backward read after filling the page found another record, confirming a previous page exists, and the NEXT-PAGE flag is set to YES and the current page number is greater than 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system updates the page number after backward navigation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The page number is decremented by 1 (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM = CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM - 1) to reflect the user has moved one page backward

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decrement Page Number When Previous Page Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system confirms that more transaction records exist before the current page and the current page number is greater than 1, the page number is decremented by 1 to reflect the correct page position after backward navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The additional backward read after filling the page did not find another record (beginning of file reached), OR the NEXT-PAGE flag is YES but the current page number is not greater than 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines the current page is the first page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The page number is set to 1 (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM = 1) to indicate the user is on the first page of the transaction list

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Page Number to 1 When Already at First Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When backward navigation reaches the beginning of the transaction file or the page number cannot be decremented further, the page number is set to 1 to indicate the user is viewing the first page of the transaction list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward page population is complete, the page number has been updated, and the browse on the Transaction file is still open
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes the backward page load
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system closes the browse on the Transaction file, moves the updated page number to the screen page number field (PAGENUMI), and displays the Transaction List screen with the updated transaction records and page number

all_rules.Rule_Name: End Browse and Display Updated Transaction List with Page Number
all_rules.Rule_Description: After completing the backward page load, the system closes the transaction file browse, updates the page number displayed on screen, and sends the refreshed transaction list to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display a new page of transactions on the Transaction List screen, triggered either by a forward page navigation (ENTER or PF8) or a backward page navigation (PF7), and the transaction file browse has been successfully initiated without errors
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system iterates through all 10 display rows (Row Index 1 through 10 inclusive, incrementing by 1 each iteration) before populating them with new transaction data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each of the 10 rows, the system clears all four display fields to spaces: Transaction ID (TRNIDnnI), Transaction Date (TDATEnnI), Transaction Description (TDESCnnI), and Transaction Amount (TAMTnnnI), so that all 10 rows are blank and ready to receive fresh transaction data from the file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All Transaction Display Rows Before Loading New Page Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying a new page of transactions (either forward or backward navigation), all 10 transaction display rows on the Transaction List screen must be completely cleared — including Transaction ID, Transaction Date, Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount — to ensure no stale data from a previous page remains visible to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is iterating through display rows 1 to 10 to clear the Transaction List screen in preparation for a new page of data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current row index is any value from 1 to 10 (WHEN 1 through WHEN 10 in the row evaluation)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID field for that specific row (TRNID01I through TRNID10I of COTRN0AI) is set to SPACES, removing any previously displayed transaction identifier for that row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Transaction ID Field for Each Display Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the screen refresh process, the Transaction ID field for each of the 10 display rows must be individually set to spaces before new transaction data is loaded, ensuring no previously displayed Transaction ID remains on screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is iterating through display rows 1 to 10 to clear the Transaction List screen in preparation for a new page of data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current row index is any value from 1 to 10 (WHEN 1 through WHEN 10 in the row evaluation)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Date field for that specific row (TDATE01I through TDATE10I of COTRN0AI) is set to SPACES, removing any previously displayed transaction date for that row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Transaction Date Field for Each Display Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the screen refresh process, the Transaction Date field for each of the 10 display rows must be individually set to spaces before new transaction data is loaded, ensuring no previously displayed Transaction Date remains on screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is iterating through display rows 1 to 10 to clear the Transaction List screen in preparation for a new page of data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current row index is any value from 1 to 10 (WHEN 1 through WHEN 10 in the row evaluation)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Description field for that specific row (TDESC01I through TDESC10I of COTRN0AI) is set to SPACES, removing any previously displayed transaction description for that row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Transaction Description Field for Each Display Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the screen refresh process, the Transaction Description field for each of the 10 display rows must be individually set to spaces before new transaction data is loaded, ensuring no previously displayed Transaction Description remains on screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is iterating through display rows 1 to 10 to clear the Transaction List screen in preparation for a new page of data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current row index is any value from 1 to 10 (WHEN 1 through WHEN 10 in the row evaluation)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Amount field for that specific row (TAMT001I through TAMT010I of COTRN0AI) is set to SPACES, removing any previously displayed transaction amount for that row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Transaction Amount Field for Each Display Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the screen refresh process, the Transaction Amount field for each of the 10 display rows must be individually set to spaces before new transaction data is loaded, ensuring no previously displayed Transaction Amount remains on screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has just cleared all four display fields (Transaction ID, Transaction Date, Transaction Description, Transaction Amount) for the current row during the screen initialization loop
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current row index is any value from 1 to 9 (i.e., row index is not yet greater than 10)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The row index is incremented by 1 (Row Index = Row Index + 1) and the system proceeds to clear the fields of the next row, continuing the loop until the row index exceeds 10, at which point all 10 rows have been cleared and the screen is ready for new transaction data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Advance to Next Row After Clearing Current Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: The screen clearing process iterates sequentially through all 10 display rows. After clearing all four fields of the current row, the row index is incremented by 1 to move to the next row, continuing until all 10 rows have been cleared.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has triggered a forward page navigation (by pressing ENTER or PF8) on the Transaction List screen, and the transaction file browse has been successfully started without any errors (ERR-FLG is OFF) and the end-of-file condition has not been reached (TRANSACT-NOT-EOF is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins the page-forward process and is ready to populate the display rows with new transaction data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system initiates a loop starting at Row Index = 1, incrementing by 1 until Row Index exceeds 10, calling the row-clearing routine (INITIALIZE-TRAN-DATA) for each row, resulting in all 10 transaction display rows being cleared before any new data is populated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Clearing Triggered During Forward Page Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating forward through the transaction list (via ENTER key or PF8), the system must clear all 10 display rows before populating them with the next set of transactions, provided the transaction file browse was initiated successfully and no errors have occurred.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has triggered a backward page navigation (by pressing PF7) on the Transaction List screen, and the transaction file browse has been successfully started without any errors (ERR-FLG is OFF) and the end-of-file condition has not been reached (TRANSACT-NOT-EOF is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins the page-backward process and is ready to populate the display rows with the previous page's transaction data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system initiates a loop starting at Row Index = 1, incrementing by 1 until Row Index exceeds 10, calling the row-clearing routine (INITIALIZE-TRAN-DATA) for each row, resulting in all 10 transaction display rows being cleared before any new data is populated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Clearing Triggered During Backward Page Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating backward through the transaction list (via PF7), the system must clear all 10 display rows before populating them with the previous set of transactions, provided the transaction file browse was initiated successfully and no errors have occurred.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been successfully retrieved from the transaction file and contains a raw transaction amount (TRAN-AMT)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to populate a screen row with the transaction data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The raw transaction amount (TRAN-AMT) is moved into the working storage display amount field (WS-TRAN-AMT), which applies the defined sign and decimal notation formatting, making it ready for screen display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Transaction Amount for Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When populating a transaction record onto the screen, the raw transaction amount from the transaction record must be formatted into a displayable amount value before being placed on the screen row.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been retrieved and contains an origination timestamp (TRAN-ORIG-TS) in internal storage format
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to populate a screen row with the transaction data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The origination timestamp is moved into the working storage timestamp field (WS-TIMESTAMP); the year component (positions 3-4 of the date portion) is extracted into WS-CURDATE-YY; the month component is extracted into WS-CURDATE-MM; the day component is extracted into WS-CURDATE-DD; and these three components are combined into the MM/DD/YY formatted display date (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY), which is then stored in WS-TRAN-DATE for screen placement

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reformat Transaction Origination Date to MM/DD/YY Display Format
all_rules.Rule_Description: The transaction origination timestamp stored in the transaction record must be extracted and reformatted from its internal timestamp format into the MM/DD/YY display format before being shown on the transaction list screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been retrieved, its amount has been formatted into WS-TRAN-AMT, and its date has been reformatted into WS-TRAN-DATE, and the current screen row index (WS-IDX) is 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the screen row for this transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID (TRAN-ID) is placed into screen row 1 Transaction ID field (TRNID01I of COTRN0AI); the formatted date (WS-TRAN-DATE) is placed into screen row 1 date field (TDATE01I of COTRN0AI); the transaction description (TRAN-DESC) is placed into screen row 1 description field (TDESC01I of COTRN0AI); the formatted amount (WS-TRAN-AMT) is placed into screen row 1 amount field (TAMT001I of COTRN0AI); AND the Transaction ID is also saved into the pagination anchor field CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST, which is used as the starting reference point when the user navigates backward to the previous page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Row 1 and Record First Transaction ID for Backward Pagination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the first transaction slot (row 1) on the transaction list screen is being filled, the transaction details are placed into screen row 1 fields AND the transaction ID is additionally saved as the first transaction ID anchor point to support backward page navigation (PF7).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been retrieved, its amount has been formatted into WS-TRAN-AMT, and its date has been reformatted into WS-TRAN-DATE, and the current screen row index (WS-IDX) is between 2 and 9 inclusive
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the screen row for this transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For the matching row index (2 through 9), the Transaction ID (TRAN-ID) is placed into the corresponding screen row Transaction ID field (TRNIDxxI of COTRN0AI); the formatted date (WS-TRAN-DATE) is placed into the corresponding screen row date field (TDATExxI of COTRN0AI); the transaction description (TRAN-DESC) is placed into the corresponding screen row description field (TDESCxxI of COTRN0AI); and the formatted amount (WS-TRAN-AMT) is placed into the corresponding screen row amount field (TAMTxxxI of COTRN0AI); no pagination anchor fields are updated for rows 2 through 9

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Rows 2 Through 9 with Transaction Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: For transactions placed in screen rows 2 through 9, the transaction details (ID, date, description, amount) are placed into the corresponding screen row fields. No pagination anchor is recorded for these rows.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been retrieved, its amount has been formatted into WS-TRAN-AMT, and its date has been reformatted into WS-TRAN-DATE, and the current screen row index (WS-IDX) is 10
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the screen row for this transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID (TRAN-ID) is placed into screen row 10 Transaction ID field (TRNID10I of COTRN0AI); the formatted date (WS-TRAN-DATE) is placed into screen row 10 date field (TDATE10I of COTRN0AI); the transaction description (TRAN-DESC) is placed into screen row 10 description field (TDESC10I of COTRN0AI); the formatted amount (WS-TRAN-AMT) is placed into screen row 10 amount field (TAMT010I of COTRN0AI); AND the Transaction ID is also saved into the pagination anchor field CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST, which is used as the starting reference point when the user navigates forward to the next page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Row 10 and Record Last Transaction ID for Forward Pagination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the tenth and final transaction slot (row 10) on the transaction list screen is being filled, the transaction details are placed into screen row 10 fields AND the transaction ID is additionally saved as the last transaction ID anchor point to support forward page navigation (PF8).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been retrieved and formatted, and the current screen row index (WS-IDX) is any value other than 1 through 10
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to populate a screen row for this transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: No transaction data is written to any screen field; no pagination anchor fields are updated; and processing continues normally without any error or message being raised

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Action for Out-of-Range Screen Row Index
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the screen row index falls outside the valid range of 1 to 10 during transaction population, no data is written to any screen field and processing continues without error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been successfully retrieved from the Transaction file, and the raw transaction amount (TRAN-AMT) is available from that record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the transaction data for display on the Transaction List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The raw transaction amount (TRAN-AMT) is moved into the formatted working storage field (WS-TRAN-AMT), which applies a display mask that includes a sign indicator (to distinguish credits from debits) and decimal notation, producing a human-readable formatted amount ready for screen placement

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Amount Sign and Decimal Formatting for Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction record is being prepared for display on the Transaction List screen, the raw transaction amount must be formatted with a sign indicator and decimal notation before it can be placed on the screen. This ensures that credit and debit amounts are visually distinguishable and decimal values are correctly represented to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction amount has been formatted with sign and decimal notation into WS-TRAN-AMT, and the current row index (WS-IDX) is 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assigns the formatted amount to the appropriate screen display field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted transaction amount (WS-TRAN-AMT) is placed into screen row 1 amount field (TAMT001) on the Transaction List screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Formatted Transaction Amount Placement into Correct Screen Row 1
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the transaction amount has been formatted, it must be placed into the correct row on the Transaction List screen. When the transaction being processed is the first record in the current page (row index = 1), the formatted amount is assigned to screen row 1 (TAMT001).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction amount has been formatted with sign and decimal notation into WS-TRAN-AMT, and the current row index (WS-IDX) is 2
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assigns the formatted amount to the appropriate screen display field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted transaction amount (WS-TRAN-AMT) is placed into screen row 2 amount field (TAMT002) on the Transaction List screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Formatted Transaction Amount Placement into Correct Screen Row 2
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the transaction amount has been formatted, it must be placed into the correct row on the Transaction List screen. When the transaction being processed is the second record in the current page (row index = 2), the formatted amount is assigned to screen row 2 (TAMT002).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction amount has been formatted with sign and decimal notation into WS-TRAN-AMT, and the current row index (WS-IDX) is 3
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assigns the formatted amount to the appropriate screen display field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted transaction amount (WS-TRAN-AMT) is placed into screen row 3 amount field (TAMT003) on the Transaction List screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Formatted Transaction Amount Placement into Correct Screen Row 3
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the transaction amount has been formatted, it must be placed into the correct row on the Transaction List screen. When the transaction being processed is the third record in the current page (row index = 3), the formatted amount is assigned to screen row 3 (TAMT003).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction amount has been formatted with sign and decimal notation into WS-TRAN-AMT, and the current row index (WS-IDX) is 4
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assigns the formatted amount to the appropriate screen display field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted transaction amount (WS-TRAN-AMT) is placed into screen row 4 amount field (TAMT004) on the Transaction List screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Formatted Transaction Amount Placement into Correct Screen Row 4
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the transaction amount has been formatted, it must be placed into the correct row on the Transaction List screen. When the transaction being processed is the fourth record in the current page (row index = 4), the formatted amount is assigned to screen row 4 (TAMT004).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction amount has been formatted with sign and decimal notation into WS-TRAN-AMT, and the current row index (WS-IDX) is 5
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assigns the formatted amount to the appropriate screen display field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted transaction amount (WS-TRAN-AMT) is placed into screen row 5 amount field (TAMT005) on the Transaction List screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Formatted Transaction Amount Placement into Correct Screen Row 5
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the transaction amount has been formatted, it must be placed into the correct row on the Transaction List screen. When the transaction being processed is the fifth record in the current page (row index = 5), the formatted amount is assigned to screen row 5 (TAMT005).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction amount has been formatted with sign and decimal notation into WS-TRAN-AMT, and the current row index (WS-IDX) is 6
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assigns the formatted amount to the appropriate screen display field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted transaction amount (WS-TRAN-AMT) is placed into screen row 6 amount field (TAMT006) on the Transaction List screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Formatted Transaction Amount Placement into Correct Screen Row 6
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the transaction amount has been formatted, it must be placed into the correct row on the Transaction List screen. When the transaction being processed is the sixth record in the current page (row index = 6), the formatted amount is assigned to screen row 6 (TAMT006).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction amount has been formatted with sign and decimal notation into WS-TRAN-AMT, and the current row index (WS-IDX) is 7
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assigns the formatted amount to the appropriate screen display field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted transaction amount (WS-TRAN-AMT) is placed into screen row 7 amount field (TAMT007) on the Transaction List screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Formatted Transaction Amount Placement into Correct Screen Row 7
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the transaction amount has been formatted, it must be placed into the correct row on the Transaction List screen. When the transaction being processed is the seventh record in the current page (row index = 7), the formatted amount is assigned to screen row 7 (TAMT007).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction amount has been formatted with sign and decimal notation into WS-TRAN-AMT, and the current row index (WS-IDX) is 8
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assigns the formatted amount to the appropriate screen display field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted transaction amount (WS-TRAN-AMT) is placed into screen row 8 amount field (TAMT008) on the Transaction List screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Formatted Transaction Amount Placement into Correct Screen Row 8
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the transaction amount has been formatted, it must be placed into the correct row on the Transaction List screen. When the transaction being processed is the eighth record in the current page (row index = 8), the formatted amount is assigned to screen row 8 (TAMT008).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction amount has been formatted with sign and decimal notation into WS-TRAN-AMT, and the current row index (WS-IDX) is 9
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assigns the formatted amount to the appropriate screen display field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted transaction amount (WS-TRAN-AMT) is placed into screen row 9 amount field (TAMT009) on the Transaction List screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Formatted Transaction Amount Placement into Correct Screen Row 9
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the transaction amount has been formatted, it must be placed into the correct row on the Transaction List screen. When the transaction being processed is the ninth record in the current page (row index = 9), the formatted amount is assigned to screen row 9 (TAMT009).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction amount has been formatted with sign and decimal notation into WS-TRAN-AMT, and the current row index (WS-IDX) is 10
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assigns the formatted amount to the appropriate screen display field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted transaction amount (WS-TRAN-AMT) is placed into screen row 10 amount field (TAMT010) on the Transaction List screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Formatted Transaction Amount Placement into Correct Screen Row 10
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the transaction amount has been formatted, it must be placed into the correct row on the Transaction List screen. When the transaction being processed is the tenth and final record in the current page (row index = 10), the formatted amount is assigned to screen row 10 (TAMT010).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been successfully retrieved from the Transaction file, and the record contains a populated Transaction Origination Timestamp (TRAN-ORIG-TS) field representing when the transaction originally occurred
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to populate the transaction data for screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies the Transaction Origination Timestamp (TRAN-ORIG-TS) from the transaction record into the working timestamp structure (WS-TIMESTAMP), making all date and time components available for individual field extraction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Load Transaction Origination Timestamp for Date Formatting
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before the transaction date can be formatted for display, the system must retrieve the transaction's original timestamp from the transaction record and stage it into a working date/time structure for subsequent field extraction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Origination Timestamp has been loaded into the working timestamp structure (WS-TIMESTAMP), and the timestamp contains a parseable Month component (WS-TIMESTAMP-DT-MM)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system extracts individual date components from the working timestamp for date reformatting
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies the two-digit Month value (WS-TIMESTAMP-DT-MM) from the working timestamp into the current date Month field (WS-CURDATE-MM), making it available for assembly into the final display date format

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Month Component from Transaction Timestamp
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system extracts the two-digit Month (MM) component from the staged transaction origination timestamp to be used as part of the formatted display date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Origination Timestamp has been loaded into the working timestamp structure (WS-TIMESTAMP), and the timestamp contains a parseable Day component (WS-TIMESTAMP-DT-DD)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system extracts individual date components from the working timestamp for date reformatting
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies the two-digit Day value (WS-TIMESTAMP-DT-DD) from the working timestamp into the current date Day field (WS-CURDATE-DD), making it available for assembly into the final display date format

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Day Component from Transaction Timestamp
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system extracts the two-digit Day (DD) component from the staged transaction origination timestamp to be used as part of the formatted display date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Origination Timestamp has been loaded into the working timestamp structure (WS-TIMESTAMP), and the timestamp contains a four-digit Year component (WS-TIMESTAMP-DT-YYYY) such as '2024'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system extracts the year component from the working timestamp for date reformatting
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system extracts only the last two characters of the four-digit year by using a substring starting at position 3 with a length of 2 (WS-TIMESTAMP-DT-YYYY(3:2)), copies this two-digit year value into the current date Year field (WS-CURDATE-YY) — for example, '2024' becomes '24' — discarding the century portion entirely

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Two-Digit Year Component from Transaction Timestamp
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system extracts only the last two digits of the four-digit Year (YYYY) from the transaction origination timestamp. The first two digits (century) are discarded, and only positions 3 and 4 of the four-digit year are used to produce the two-digit year (YY) for display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Month (WS-CURDATE-MM), Day (WS-CURDATE-DD), and two-digit Year (WS-CURDATE-YY) components have all been individually extracted from the transaction origination timestamp and are populated in their respective working fields, and these three components are combined within the composite date field WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY in MM/DD/YY order
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes the transaction date value for screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system moves the assembled composite date (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) into the transaction display date field (WS-TRAN-DATE) in MM/DD/YY format, which is then mapped to the corresponding transaction row date field on the Transaction List screen (e.g., TDATE01I through TDATE10I depending on the row position 1–10)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assemble Transaction Date into MM/DD/YY Display Format
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all individual date components (Month, Day, two-digit Year) have been extracted from the transaction origination timestamp, the system assembles them into the final MM/DD/YY formatted date string that will be displayed on the Transaction List screen next to each transaction row.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction list page is being populated and the current row index being filled is row 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A transaction record is read and assigned to display row 1 of the transaction list screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID of that record must be placed into screen display row 1 (TRNID01I) AND simultaneously saved as the First Transaction ID on the page (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST) to serve as the backward navigation anchor for PF7 scrolling

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save First Transaction ID on Page as Backward Navigation Anchor
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the first row (row 1) of the transaction list page is being populated, the system must record the Transaction ID both in the first screen display row and as the page's first transaction anchor (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST), which will be used as the starting reference point when the user navigates backward using PF7.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction list page is being populated and the current row index being filled is any row between 2 and 9 (inclusive)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A transaction record is read and assigned to a middle display row (rows 2 through 9) of the transaction list screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID of that record must be placed only into the corresponding screen display row field (TRNID02I through TRNID09I respectively), and neither the First Transaction ID anchor (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST) nor the Last Transaction ID anchor (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST) is updated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Middle Transaction Rows Without Updating Navigation Anchors
all_rules.Rule_Description: When rows 2 through 9 of the transaction list page are being populated, the system places the Transaction ID only into the corresponding screen display row. No navigation anchor values are updated for these middle rows.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction list page is being populated and the current row index being filled is row 10
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A transaction record is read and assigned to display row 10 of the transaction list screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID of that record must be placed into screen display row 10 (TRNID10I) AND simultaneously saved as the Last Transaction ID on the page (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST) to serve as the forward navigation anchor for PF8 scrolling

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Last Transaction ID on Page as Forward Navigation Anchor
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the last row (row 10) of the transaction list page is being populated, the system must record the Transaction ID both in the tenth screen display row and as the page's last transaction anchor (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST), which will be used as the starting reference point when the user navigates forward using PF8.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the transaction list and the current page has a saved First Transaction ID (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST) from when the page was populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF7 to navigate to the previous page AND the current page number is greater than 1
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must use the saved First Transaction ID (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST) as the starting position (TRAN-ID) for reading records backward; if the First Transaction ID is blank or empty, the system defaults to starting from the very beginning of the transaction file (LOW-VALUES), and then proceeds to retrieve the previous page of up to 10 transactions

all_rules.Rule_Name: Use First Transaction ID Anchor as Starting Point for Backward Page Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF7 to scroll backward to the previous page, the system uses the saved First Transaction ID of the current page (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST) as the reference point from which to begin reading records in reverse order. If no first transaction ID has been saved, the system starts from the very beginning of the transaction file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the transaction list and the current page has a saved Last Transaction ID (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST) from when the page was populated, and the next-page indicator confirms more pages are available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF8 to navigate to the next page AND the next-page-available indicator is set to YES
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must use the saved Last Transaction ID (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST) as the starting position (TRAN-ID) for reading records forward; if the Last Transaction ID is blank or empty, the system defaults to starting from the highest possible transaction value (HIGH-VALUES), and then proceeds to retrieve the next page of up to 10 transactions

all_rules.Rule_Name: Use Last Transaction ID Anchor as Starting Point for Forward Page Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF8 to scroll forward to the next page, the system uses the saved Last Transaction ID of the current page (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-LAST) as the reference point from which to begin reading records in forward order. If no last transaction ID has been saved, the system starts from the highest possible transaction value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed the loop to load up to 10 transactions for the current page from the transaction file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end-of-file indicator for the transaction file is NOT set (TRANSACT-NOT-EOF is true) AND no error condition is active (ERR-FLG-OFF is true) after the loading loop completes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system determines that a full page of 10 transactions has been successfully loaded and proceeds to attempt reading one additional record beyond the current page to check for more data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine If Current Page Is Fully Loaded with 10 Transactions
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to load transactions onto the current page, the system checks whether a full page of 10 transactions was successfully retrieved without reaching the end of the transaction file, to decide whether to probe for additional records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A full page of 10 transactions has been successfully loaded and the transaction file has not reached end-of-file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to read the next sequential transaction record from the transaction file beyond the 10th record of the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system uses the result of this read (success or end-of-file) exclusively to set the next-page availability indicator, and the record read is not displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Probe for Additional Transaction Record Beyond Current Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: After confirming a full page of 10 transactions is loaded, the system reads one extra record from the transaction file solely to determine whether more transactions exist beyond the current page, without displaying that record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A full page of 10 transactions has been loaded and the system has attempted to read one additional record beyond the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The additional read is successful — the transaction file end-of-file indicator remains NOT set (TRANSACT-NOT-EOF is true) AND no error condition is active (ERR-FLG-OFF is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next-page indicator is set to YES (NEXT-PAGE-YES), signaling that more transactions are available and the user may navigate forward to the next page using PF8

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Next Page Available When Additional Transaction Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the probe read beyond the current page successfully retrieves a record, the system marks that a next page of transactions is available, enabling the user to scroll forward.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A full page of 10 transactions has been loaded and the system has attempted to read one additional record beyond the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The additional read reaches the end of the transaction file — the end-of-file indicator is set (TRANSACT-EOF becomes true) OR an error condition is active
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next-page indicator is set to NO (NEXT-PAGE-NO), signaling that the current page is the last page and the user cannot navigate further forward

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Next Page Unavailable When No Additional Transaction Exists After Full Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the probe read beyond a full page of 10 transactions reaches the end of the transaction file, the system marks that no further pages are available, preventing the user from attempting to scroll forward.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed the loop to load up to 10 transactions and the transaction file end-of-file was reached OR an error occurred before 10 records were loaded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end-of-file indicator is set (TRANSACT-EOF is true) OR an error condition is active (ERR-FLG-ON is true), meaning fewer than 10 records were loaded — regardless of whether the row index (WS-IDX) is greater than 1 (at least 1 record loaded) or equal to 1 (no records loaded)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next-page indicator is set to NO (NEXT-PAGE-NO), signaling that no further pages exist beyond the current partial or empty page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Next Page Unavailable When Partial or Empty Page Loaded
all_rules.Rule_Description: When fewer than 10 transactions are loaded (partial page) or no transactions are loaded at all (empty page), the system unconditionally marks that no next page is available, regardless of whether any records were retrieved.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction file reached end-of-file or an error occurred before a full page of 10 transactions was loaded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The row index (WS-IDX) is greater than 1, meaning at least one transaction record was successfully loaded onto the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by 1 to reflect that the user has moved to a new page, and the next-page indicator is set to NO

all_rules.Rule_Name: Increment Page Number When at Least One Transaction Record Was Loaded on Partial Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a partial page is loaded (at least one but fewer than 10 transactions), the system still increments the page counter to reflect that the user has advanced to a new page, even though it is not fully populated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The loading loop has completed and the transaction file end-of-file indicator is NOT set (TRANSACT-NOT-EOF is true) AND no error condition is active (ERR-FLG-OFF is true), confirming 10 records were loaded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms a full page of 10 transactions has been loaded
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by 1 (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM = CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM + 1) before the probe read is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Increment Page Number After Successfully Loading a Full Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a full page of 10 transactions is confirmed as loaded, the system increments the page counter before probing for additional records, ensuring the displayed page number accurately reflects the user's current position in the transaction list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the transaction list and the current page number is tracked in the session context (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM), and the system has started a forward browse of the transaction file from the current Transaction ID position
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system successfully reads and loads all 10 transaction records into the display rows (WS-IDX reaches 11, meaning the loop completed with records still available and no end-of-file condition was reached), indicating a full page was populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number is incremented by 1 (Page = Page + 1), and the updated page number is displayed on the Transaction List screen in the page number field (PAGENUMI)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Increment Page Number When Full Page of 10 Transactions Loaded (Forward Navigation)
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating forward and a full page of 10 transactions is successfully retrieved from the transaction file, the current page number is incremented by 1 to reflect the new page position.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is navigating forward through the transaction list and the current page number is tracked in the session context (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM), and the system has started a forward browse of the transaction file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reaches the end of the transaction file before loading all 10 records (TRANSACT-EOF is set), but at least 1 transaction record was loaded into the display (WS-IDX is greater than 1, meaning the index advanced at least once from its starting value of 1)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number is incremented by 1 (Page = Page + 1), the next-page indicator is set to NO (no further forward navigation is possible), and the updated page number is displayed on the Transaction List screen in the page number field (PAGENUMI)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Increment Page Number When Partial Page of Transactions Loaded at End of File (Forward Navigation)
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating forward and the end of the transaction file is reached before filling all 10 rows, but at least 1 transaction was loaded, the page number is still incremented by 1 to reflect that a new (partial) page has been reached.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is navigating forward through the transaction list and the current page number is tracked in the session context (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM), and the system has started a forward browse of the transaction file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reaches the end of the transaction file immediately without loading any transaction records (TRANSACT-EOF is set and WS-IDX remains at 1, meaning no records were populated into any display row)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number is NOT incremented and remains unchanged, the next-page indicator is set to NO, and the unchanged page number is displayed on the Transaction List screen in the page number field (PAGENUMI)

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Page Number Change When No Transactions Found During Forward Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating forward and no transaction records are found at all (end of file is reached immediately with zero records loaded), the page number remains unchanged.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is navigating backward through the transaction list using PF7, and the current page number stored in the session context (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM) is greater than 1, and the system has started a backward browse of the transaction file from the first Transaction ID of the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: After loading up to 10 transactions backward into the display rows, the system successfully reads one additional previous transaction record beyond the loaded page (TRANSACT-NOT-EOF is true and no error flag is set), confirming that prior records exist before the current page, AND the current page number is greater than 1
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number is decremented by 1 (Page = Page - 1), and the updated page number is displayed on the Transaction List screen in the page number field (PAGENUMI)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decrement Page Number When Prior Transactions Exist Beyond Current Page (Backward Navigation)
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating backward and there are more transactions before the current page (i.e., the user is not on the first page), the page number is decremented by 1 to reflect moving to the previous page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is navigating backward through the transaction list using PF7, and the current page number stored in the session context (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM) is exactly 1, and the system has started a backward browse of the transaction file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: After loading transactions backward, the system successfully reads one additional previous transaction record (TRANSACT-NOT-EOF is true and no error flag is set), confirming prior records exist, BUT the current page number is NOT greater than 1 (it is already at page 1)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The page number is set to 1 (Page = 1), ensuring it does not go below the minimum page value, and the page number 1 is displayed on the Transaction List screen in the page number field (PAGENUMI)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Page Number to 1 When Already on First Page During Backward Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating backward and prior records exist beyond the loaded page but the current page number is already 1, the page number is reset to 1 to ensure it never goes below the minimum value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is navigating backward through the transaction list using PF7, and the current page number is tracked in the session context (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM), and the system has started a backward browse of the transaction file from the first Transaction ID of the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: After loading up to 10 transactions backward into the display rows, the system attempts to read one additional previous transaction record but reaches the beginning of the file (TRANSACT-EOF is set or an error condition is encountered), confirming no prior records exist before the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The page number is set to 1 (Page = 1), confirming the user is on the first page, and the page number 1 is displayed on the Transaction List screen in the page number field (PAGENUMI)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Page Number to 1 When No Prior Transactions Exist During Backward Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating backward and no transactions exist before the currently displayed page (the beginning of the transaction file has been reached), the page number is reset to 1, confirming the user is on the first page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has performed a navigation action (ENTER for new search, PF7 for backward, or PF8 for forward) and the page number has been computed or adjusted accordingly in the session context (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes the page number calculation (increment, decrement, reset to 1, or no change) and prepares to send the Transaction List screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The computed page number value from the session context (CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM) is moved into the page number display field (PAGENUMI) on the Transaction List screen (COTRN0AI), and the screen is sent to the user showing the correct current page number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Updated Page Number on Transaction List Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After any page navigation action (forward or backward), the current page number is always displayed on the Transaction List screen so the user knows their current position in the transaction list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction List screen with an active session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Main Menu screen identified as 'COMEN01C'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Main Menu as Return Destination on PF3
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 on the Transaction List screen, the system designates the Main Menu screen (COMEN01C) as the target destination for navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is about to transfer control to a destination program after PF3 is pressed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The destination program value is evaluated and found to be blank (spaces) or uninitialized (low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system overrides the destination and sets it to the Sign-On screen identified as 'COSGN00C' to ensure a valid navigation target

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Destination Program Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to any screen, the system validates that a destination program has been properly set. If the destination is blank or uninitialized, the system defaults to the Sign-On screen to prevent navigation to an undefined target.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is processing a return-to-previous-screen request and the destination program has been found to be blank or uninitialized
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The destination program field contains spaces or low-values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Sign-On screen identified as 'COSGN00C', overriding any previously blank or invalid destination value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Navigation to Sign-On Screen When Destination is Invalid
all_rules.Rule_Description: As a fallback policy, when no valid destination program is defined at the time of navigation, the system routes the user to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) rather than allowing navigation to fail or reach an undefined screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has a valid destination program set (either COMEN01C or defaulted to COSGN00C) and is preparing to transfer control
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is about to execute the screen transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the current transaction identifier into the session data field 'From Transaction ID', records the current program name into the session data field 'From Program', and resets the program context indicator to zero (0) in the session data before transferring control

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Program and Transaction in Session Data Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to another screen, the system records the current program name and current transaction identifier into the shared session data (communication area), along with resetting the program context to zero, so the destination screen knows where the user navigated from.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination program has been validated or defaulted, and the current program name, transaction ID, and program context have been recorded in the session data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the screen transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system transfers complete control to the destination program (COMEN01C for Main Menu, or COSGN00C as fallback) and passes the full session data (communication area containing From Transaction ID, From Program, and Program Context) to the destination screen, ending execution of the current Transaction List program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Destination Screen with Session Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: After recording the originating program and transaction details, the system transfers full control to the destination screen (Main Menu COMEN01C or Sign-On COSGN00C as fallback), passing the complete session data so the destination screen has full context of the user's session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction List screen and has an active session with a valid communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any function key other than Enter, PF3, PF7, or PF8
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies the key press as unrecognized and does not perform any transaction retrieval, navigation, or selection processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Unrecognized Function Key Press on Transaction List Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses a function key that is not one of the four recognized keys (Enter, PF3, PF7, PF8) on the Transaction List screen, the system must identify it as an invalid key action and prevent any transaction list processing from occurring.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction List screen and has pressed an unrecognized function key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the pressed key and determines it does not match Enter, PF3, PF7, or PF8
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error indicator flag to 'Y' (active error state) to mark that an invalid key error condition has occurred

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Error Indicator on Invalid Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unrecognized function key is pressed, the system must activate the error indicator flag to signal that an error condition exists, which will control subsequent screen display behavior.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error indicator has been set to active due to an unrecognized function key press on the Transaction List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to re-display the Transaction List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the error message field with the standard invalid key message (sourced from the application message constant CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) to be shown to the user on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Invalid Key Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unrecognized function key is pressed, the system must populate the screen error message area with the standard invalid key message to inform the user that their key press was not recognized.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error indicator is active and the invalid key error message has been set, and the screen erase flag is set to YES (default initial state)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs the send transaction list screen operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the Transaction List screen (map COTRN0A from mapset COTRN00) with the invalid key error message visible in the error message area, with the cursor positioned on the Transaction ID input field, and the screen is refreshed with an erase so the user can see the error and retry with a valid key

all_rules.Rule_Name: Re-Display Transaction List Screen with Invalid Key Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: After detecting an invalid key press and setting the error message, the system must re-display the Transaction List screen showing the error message to the user, preserving the current screen content so the user can take a valid action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Return to Previous Screen process has been triggered AND the target program name stored in the session communication area (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is either blank (SPACES) or contains no value (LOW-VALUES)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the target program name before transferring control
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the target program name to 'COSGN00C' (Sign-On Screen) as the default navigation destination, overriding the blank or null value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Navigation Target to Sign-On Screen When No Target Is Set
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the return-to-previous-screen process is triggered but no target program has been specified in the session, the system defaults the navigation destination to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) to ensure the user is always directed to a valid screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Return to Previous Screen process has been triggered AND the target program name has been confirmed (either defaulted to COSGN00C or already set to COMEN01C)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the session communication area for the screen transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must record the current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) into the session communication area field CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, preserving the originating transaction context for the receiving program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Transaction ID in Session Data Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to any previous screen, the system captures and stores the current transaction identifier into the session communication area so the receiving program knows which transaction initiated the navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Return to Previous Screen process has been triggered AND the current Transaction ID has already been recorded in the session communication area (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system continues preparing the session communication area for the screen transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must record the current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME) into the session communication area field CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, preserving the originating program identity for the receiving program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Program Name in Session Data Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to any previous screen, the system captures and stores the current program name into the session communication area so the receiving program knows which program initiated the navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Return to Previous Screen process has been triggered AND both the current Transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) and Program Name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) have been recorded in the session communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes the session communication area before the screen transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the program context value (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) to zero (0), clearing any prior operational context so the target program initializes in a clean state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Program Context to Zero Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to any previous screen, the system resets the program context indicator to zero in the session communication area, ensuring the receiving program starts without any inherited operational context from the current program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Return to Previous Screen process has been triggered AND the target program is determined to be 'COSGN00C' — either because EIBCALEN equals zero (no active session exists) OR because the target program name was blank/null and defaulted to COSGN00C AND the session communication area has been updated with the current Transaction ID, Program Name, and Program Context reset to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the navigation transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must transfer full control to the Sign-On screen program 'COSGN00C', passing the complete session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), and the current program must terminate its execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Sign-On Screen When No Active Session or Default Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user has no active session (first-time entry with no communication area) or when the navigation target defaults to the Sign-On screen, the system transfers full control to the Sign-On program (COSGN00C), passing the complete session communication area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction List screen AND the user has pressed PF3 (Return to Menu key) AND the target program has been set to 'COMEN01C' in the session communication area AND the session communication area has been updated with the current Transaction ID, Program Name, and Program Context reset to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the navigation transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must transfer full control to the Main Menu screen program 'COMEN01C', passing the complete session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), and the current program must terminate its execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Main Menu Screen When User Presses PF3
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user explicitly presses PF3 to return to the main menu, the system transfers full control to the Main Menu program (COMEN01C), passing the complete session communication area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction List screen is active, a browse of the Transaction file has been successfully started using the reference Transaction ID (last Transaction ID from the current page when PF8 is pressed, or first Transaction ID when navigating forward from ENTER), and the system is about to load up to 10 transactions for the new page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key pressed by the user is NOT ENTER, NOT PF7, and NOT PF3 (i.e., the user pressed PF8 to scroll forward to the next page)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system reads and discards the next transaction record from the Transaction file, advancing the browse position past the starting Transaction ID, so that the transaction already seen at the bottom of the previous page is not repeated at the top of the new page; after this skip, the system proceeds to populate up to 10 transaction rows for the new page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Starting Transaction ID When Scrolling Forward via PF8
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user navigates forward through the transaction list using PF8, the system uses the last Transaction ID from the current page as the starting browse position. To avoid displaying that same transaction again at the top of the next page, the system advances past it by reading the next record before beginning to populate the new page. When the user presses ENTER or PF7 (or PF3), no skip occurs and the page is populated starting from the current browse position.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing a page of transactions on the Transaction List screen, and the system has retained the Transaction ID of the first record displayed on the current page (CDEMO-CT00-TRNID-FIRST)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF7 to navigate to the previous page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the first Transaction ID of the current page is available (not spaces or null), the system sets the browse starting position (TRAN-ID) to that first Transaction ID; if the first Transaction ID is blank or null, the system sets the browse starting position to the beginning of the transaction file (LOW-VALUES), and in both cases the browse cursor is positioned at that starting point in the transaction file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Backward Browse Starting Position to First Transaction of Current Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user navigates backward (PF7), the system must position the transaction file browse cursor at the first transaction ID that was displayed on the current page, so that backward reading begins from the correct reference point. If no first transaction ID is recorded, the system defaults to the beginning of the transaction file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction List screen viewing a page of transactions, the browse cursor has been positioned at the first Transaction ID of the current page, and no errors have occurred during browse positioning
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key pressed is PF7 (i.e., the key pressed is NOT Enter and NOT PF8)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system reads one record backward from the current browse position to move past the boundary record (the first record of the current page), so that subsequent backward reads will load the correct set of transactions belonging to the previous page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Boundary Record When Navigating Backward via PF7
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF7 to go to the previous page, the browse cursor is initially positioned at the first transaction of the current page (which is a boundary record already seen). The system must read one record backward past this boundary record before beginning to load the previous page's transactions, ensuring the current page's first record is not re-displayed on the previous page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward page navigation process has been initiated and the browse cursor has been successfully positioned at the reference Transaction ID with no errors
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key pressed by the user is Enter (DFHENTER) or PF8 (DFHPF8)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does NOT read a backward boundary record and instead proceeds directly to clearing the transaction display rows and loading up to 10 transactions backward from the current browse position

all_rules.Rule_Name: Bypass Boundary Skip When Navigation Context Is Not PF7
all_rules.Rule_Description: The decision to skip the boundary record during backward page navigation is conditional on the key that triggered the navigation. If the navigation was triggered by Enter or PF8 (not PF7), the system does not perform the backward boundary skip and proceeds directly to loading the previous page records from the current browse position.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction List screen is displayed with up to 10 transaction rows, and the user has the ability to enter a selection value next to any transaction row
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user enters a non-blank value in the selection field of Row 1 (SEL0001I) and presses ENTER
